subject: gov.policy
name: Cost to Communicate Roadmap
milestone: Market analysis study put out to tender, reported 2026-08-01
position_start: Did not exist; no successor instrument after the 2019 Data Services Market Inquiry
position_end: Study out to tender; no roadmap published
note: the DCDT tender concedes a "current policy vacuum" and that the price benefits expected from the 2022 spectrum auction "remain largely unmet", naming market concentration, spectrum allocation and the burden on prepaid consumers as structural causes; deliverables are a Cost to Communicate Roadmap of short-, medium- and long-term reforms plus an assessment of ICASA's measures and of progress implementing the Competition Commission's 2019 Data Services Market Inquiry recommendations; the tender's issue date is not stated, so as_at is month-precision

subject: gov.policy
name: Determination and Directive on the Implementation of Data Governance in the Public Service
milestone: Issued by the public service minister
position_end: A determination and directive of the public service minister requiring departments to implement data governance, with provisions for managing non-compliance

subject: gov.policy
name: Determination and Directive on the Usage of Cloud Computing Services in the Public Service
milestone: Issued by the public service minister, 2022
position_end: A determination and directive of the public service minister requiring departments to complete a risk assessment, a business case and a readiness checklist before acquiring any cloud service, with provisions for managing non-compliance
note: the text carries no signature date; it takes effect on the minister's signature

subject: gov.policy
name: Discussion document on subsidies for needy persons
position_end: The universal service agency published a discussion document under section 88 of the Electronic Communications Act on which needy persons should receive electronic communications subsidies, who must apply and to whom subsidies may be paid; it sets six provisional propositions with financial inability as the central test, and proposes no income threshold, benefit amount or payment platform
note: a separate notice from the review of the universal access determination

subject: gov.policy
name: ICT and Digital Economy Masterplan
milestone: A digital economy framework and strategy planned for Cabinet in 2023/24
position_end: A final draft of February 2021 set four big bets, five enablers and targets of R200bn a year and one million jobs; an outside assessment in 2023 marked the country down because only drafts were public, and the department's 2023/24 plan put a digital economy framework and strategy to Cabinet that year; no adopted text is held

subject: gov.policy
name: ICT indicators and scenario-modelling system to 2050
position_end: Tendered by the communications department to steer the digital economy to 2050, framed against the National Digital Transformation Roadmap, the Presidential Commission on the Fourth Industrial Revolution and the Digital Economy Masterplan; no award, value or delivery date published
note: A tender, not a system: nothing is built or awarded.

subject: gov.policy
name: Mega infrastructure project monitoring dashboard
position_end: A joint push by the Presidency and the planning and evaluation department to fast-track a digital dashboard monitoring mega infrastructure projects, put before the parliamentary committee on the Presidency alongside a wider review of progress against the state-of-the-nation commitments
note: no delivery date, data source, custodian or statement of whether the dashboard will be public is given

subject: gov.policy
name: National AI policy
milestone: Cabinet to finalise the replacement before end-March 2027, consultation from April, stated 2026-10-15
position_end: The draft policy gazetted for comment, proposing a national artificial-intelligence commission, an ethics board, a regulatory authority and a safety institute on a phased implementation, and later withdrawn in its entirety; a survey of Eastern Cape schools found 4 per cent with an artificial-intelligence policy while 48 per cent of South African teachers already use the tools; the deputy minister said the final redraft is due for ministerial input before the end of November 2026 and at cabinet by the end of the 2026/27 financial year. On 2026-10-15 the minister said cabinet will finalise the replacement policy before end-March 2027, with public consultation expected from April; one of the two officials suspended over the hallucinated draft has resigned
note: the draft was withdrawn in April 2026 after AI-hallucinated citations were found in its reference list; the redraft will issue national guidelines rather than prescribe rules to industry, the seven proposed new institutions are being reconsidered, and cabinet is targeted for November 2026 with January 2027 as fallback - South Africa has no gazetted national AI policy framework as at 2026-07-29

subject: gov.policy
name: National Policy on Data and Cloud
position_end: Gazetted as final policy, the standing national instrument on data and cloud; a policy direction of December 2025 requires data sovereignty, data protection and data security to be weighed in sector ownership regulation
sources: 2024-05-31-national-policy-on-data-and-cloud|2025-12-11-policy-direction-icasa-bbbee-data-sovereignty|2025-01-01 South African Digital Sovereignty at the Crossroad of Securitization and Development (Chapter 4) - Digital Sovereignty in the BRICS Countries
note: declares that data generated in South Africa shall be the property of South Africa and provides for in-country copies for law enforcement; Research ICT Africa warns it could obstruct the cross-border flows AfCFTA needs, and it sits markedly apart from POPIA's adequacy logic

subject: gov.policy
name: Open Data Policy Framework
status: In development, framework developed; adoption not on record
milestone: Developed with a regional research institute under a continental data-policy project
position_end: An Open Data Policy Framework developed with a regional research institute under the project domesticating the African Union data policy framework; no adopted text, commencement or portal is held
note: the institute's own account

subject: gov.policy
name: Operation Vulindlela Phase II
note: approved at the same Cabinet meeting as the Roadmap; the Q1 2026/27 report concedes progress has been uneven and in certain instances slower than initially anticipated, against the 80% on track figure of 2026-04-23 which remains the dated prior

subject: gov.policy
name: Regulator inquiry into over-the-top services
position_start: Under consideration: the regulator told parliament earlier in 2026 that it was weighing a market inquiry into broadcasting over-the-top services and their effect on licensees and markets, against the audiovisual policy review
position_end: Gazetted as a section 4B market inquiry into the impact of over-the-top services on telecommunications, broadcasting and postal licensees and on the regulatory framework, run in four phases from a notice and questionnaire to findings gazetted at the close
note: two inquiries announced in the same week, neither with published terms of reference or a timetable; the communications department separately tendered for experts to run a market analysis that could precede pricing intervention

subject: gov.policy
name: Regulator inquiry into the impact of over-the-top services
status: In development, notices withdrawn for republication
position_end: The regulator withdrew both notices of its inquiry into over-the-top services on 30 September 2026 to address administrative and procedural matters, and says it will republish at a later date with more context and guidance on taking part; those who have already commented may resubmit
note: no republication date is given

subject: gov.policy
name: Review of the 2010 universal access and universal service determination
milestone: Discussion document gazetted; comments close 30 October 2026
position_end: The universal service agency opened a public consultation on whether to update the 2010 ministerial determination, with a discussion document weighing affordability, access for people with disabilities and meaningful connectivity, three options and a preliminary preference for targeted revision; it creates no new funding, subsidy or licensing obligation, and comments close on 30 October 2026

subject: gov.policy
name: Universal Service and Access Fund manual
position_start: Draft withdrawn in November 2025 and reissued for comment in February 2026
position_end: The minister approved the fund manual, which sets its objectives, governance, funding instruments and accountability, and the agency says it will now implement it; publication of the text is not reported

subject: gov.legislate
name: AfCFTA Digital Trade Protocol ratification and domestication
milestone: Tabled 30 July 2026; NCOP select committee briefed 2026-10-20
position_end: Approved by Cabinet and tabled in Parliament on 30 July 2026, with legal opinions from Justice and DIRCO finding no conflict with domestic law; the NCOP select committee was briefed on 20 October 2026, and both houses must approve before ratification
note: the presenting department is not named on the slides

subject: gov.legislate
name: Amended court rules for access-to-information applications
milestone: Justice committee agreed publication of the proposed rules, 2026-09-23
position_end: Proposed rules drafted by the Rules Board for Courts of Law standardise section 78 applications across all courts including magistrates' courts, require section 80 representations under oath at least five days before a hearing, move appeals under the general court rules and repeal the previous PAIA Rules; proposals, not in force

subject: gov.legislate
name: Breach notification rate
position_end: ~244 per month (April-August 2026), on more than 8,000 security-compromise reports received to date and 1,220 since the 2026/27 financial year opened in April; the regulator projects over 3,000 for the full year and calls the rate very alarming
note: the monthly rate has eased across the three periods held while the cumulative total and the regulator's own assessment have not; the projection is the regulator's

subject: gov.legislate
name: Capital Flow Management Regulations and Crypto Asset Manual
milestone: Pre-approval model dropped, announced in the 2026 MTBPS 2026-10-21
position_end: After thousands of comments on the draft regulations and crypto asset manual, the Treasury dropped the pre-approval model and promised a revised second draft for further comment, with no date
note: the draft regulations were proposed by National Treasury in April 2026 and would replace the pre-approval exchange-control regime with a risk-based reporting system, carrying penalties of up to R1 million, five years imprisonment or both; the draft manual sets the rules licensed crypto asset service providers would follow on cross-border transactions and what must be reported to the Reserve Bank Financial Surveillance Department; Treasury states the manual was published before it had considered the comments already submitted on the regulations, and that both remain subject to refinement

subject: gov.legislate
name: Conduct of Financial Institutions Bill
milestone: Notice of introduction to the National Assembly gazetted 2026-04-17
position_start: Draft bill awaiting Cabinet approval (as at 2026-01)
position_end: Approved by Cabinet for submission to Parliament in late March 2026, with the finance minister's notice of its introduction to the National Assembly gazetted on 17 April 2026; the conduct regulator's themed frameworks under it remain in informal consultation
note: would consolidate conduct rules including open finance and buy-now-pay-later

subject: gov.legislate
name: Copyright Amendment Bill
milestone: Judgment delivered 2026-06-26, parts returned to Parliament
position_end: The Constitutional Court held on 26 June 2026 that the fair use exception in section 12A, sections 12B and 12C, sections 12D(6) to (9) and sections 19B and 19C are constitutional within the scope of the President's referral, and declared sections 12D(1) to (5) an arbitrary deprivation of property under section 25(1) for failing to define who benefits, leaving commercial use uncertain and permitting whole textbooks to be copied on the user's own view of whether the price is reasonable; the educational-copying subsections return to Parliament for repair
note: would replace fair dealing with a broader fair use exception; Majiedt J dissented on sections 12D(1) to (5) alone and the orders apply equally to the Performers' Protection Amendment Bill; the referral of sections 6A, 7A and 8A was held incompetent because the President's reservations had already been met; the Bill says nothing explicit about generative AI or text and data mining, which imports the American judicial answer to those questions along with the doctrine

subject: gov.legislate
name: Customs Control Act and Customs Duty Act, 2014
milestone: Not promulgated, reported for April 2025 to March 2026
position_end: The modernised customs statutes of 2014 are still not promulgated, so the Customs and Excise Act of 1964 remains the law applied, which the revenue service says delays fully enabling reformed customs processes

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cybercrimes Act 19 of 2020
position_end: In force, the country's substantive cybercrime statute; the state signed the United Nations Convention against Cybercrime on 25 October 2025, and consultation on a revised National Cybersecurity Strategy is substantially complete with adoption expected in the following quarter
note: the statute is held as an excerpt; the strategy's adoption is a stated expectation and no adopted text is on file

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cybercrimes Act investigations, prosecutions and convictions
position_start: 2,679 cybercrime cases opened in 2022/23-2023/24 and 83 referred for prosecution; 37 cases carrying 88 Cybercrimes Act charges on court rolls (2024-11)
position_end: Eight cyber extortion, ransomware and related cases registered by the priority-crime directorate over three years, with one arrest, and no arrest for the 2025 Weather Service attack (2026-10)
note: the two ends count different case sets and are not a series; the prosecuting authority recorded convictions manually, without the offence

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cybersecurity Bill
milestone: State Security Agency stakeholder engagement opened December 2023
position_end: No bill published; the cybersecurity provisions were removed from the bill enacted as the Cybercrimes Act in 2021, and the State Security Agency began engaging public- and private-sector stakeholders on a Cybersecurity Bill in December 2023
note: a law firm's tracker; no government text is on file

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electoral Code of Conduct on Countering Disinformation
position_end: A gazetted code binding political parties, candidates and anyone acting on their instruction or for reward across all election-related communication, requiring accuracy checks before sharing, public retraction and correction of false information within 36 hours, clear labelling of AI-generated content and of political advertising, and reporting of online disinformation to Real411 within 36 hours; it bars fake accounts, bot networks, coordinated inauthentic behaviour, doxing and cyberbullying, and contravention carries the sanctions of the Electoral Code of Conduct under the Municipal Electoral Act 27 of 2000. It was gazetted on 4 September 2026 as General Notice 4138 in Gazette 55341; by 20 October the Commission had received more than 700 election-misinformation complaints, most linked to posts on X, and had partnered Google, Meta, Microsoft, TikTok and Moxii Africa for direct referral of disinformation
note: parties undertake to comply at the electoral code of conduct signing ceremony on 2026-09-23

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electronic Communications Amendment Bill
position_end: Tabled by the Minister of Communications and Digital Technologies on 20 April 2026; it would empower the local-government minister to make a national standard by-law on rapid deployment of electronic communications networks. The portfolio committee extended the deadline for written submissions by one month, to 4pm on Monday 21 September 2026
note: the Bill's own text is now held, which settles the licensing exemption this row could not previously state: clause 2 amends section 6 of the principal Act to make electronic communications network services provided on a not-for-profit basis licence-exempt, and clause 3 inserts a new section 21A requiring the local-government minister to make a national standard draft by-law providing, among other things, for a uniform wayleave application and approval process

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electronic Communications and Transactions Act 25 of 2002
position_end: In force as the country's electronic transactions statute, the standing legal basis for electronic contracting and data messages
note: held as an excerpt; no amendment is on file and no repeal or successor bill appears

subject: gov.legislate
name: End-user and Subscriber Service Charter Amendment Regulations
position_end: Gazetted 2026-01-23; under review application
note: GN 7027 in GG 53991, gazetted 2026-01-23 and in force 2027-01-23: unused bundles must roll over automatically and free of charge at least once, excluding bundles of seven days or less and uncapped, free and promotional bundles, with depletion alerts at 50%, 80% and 100%; MTN and Vodacom have filed for review, and the filing date and case number are unestablished

subject: gov.legislate
name: Film and Publication Board enforcement under the Films and Publications Act
milestone: R16.175m in fines announced at a media briefing, 17 September 2026
note: R16.175 million in fines on distributors found non-compliant, most of the content distributed online, and the board states the enforcement reaches distributors based abroad; the period the total covers, the number of distributors fined and the amount actually recovered are not published

subject: gov.legislate
name: Information Regulator appropriation
milestone: 2026/27 estimates enacted by Appropriation Act 10 of 2026, gazetted 2026-07-16
position_end: R140.3m (2026/27), a separately printed subprogramme of the Justice vote's Programme 5, enacted within the programme total by Appropriation Act 10 of 2026
note: the Act prints the programme total only; the subprogramme figure is the estimates'

subject: gov.legislate
name: Malabo Convention ratification position
milestone: A peer-reviewed review of four countries' health-data governance records South Africa as a non-signatory, 2026-08-14
position_end: Not held. A peer-reviewed review of health-data governance in Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda and South Africa records only Rwanda as a Malabo Convention signatory, and finds all four frameworks fragmented, with weak cross-border transfer harmonisation and capacity gaps

subject: gov.legislate
name: Media and Digital Platforms Market Inquiry remedies
milestone: Final Report and binding remedial actions published 2025-11-13
position_end: Final Report released with binding remedial actions under section 43D(1) for Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, TikTok and X; Google's Annexure 8 commitment is up to ZAR 687,500,000 over the five-year term
note: the inquiry's own Final Report and its Annexure 8 remedial actions are now held; the secondary analyst account is superseded

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Identification and Registration Bill
milestone: Revision for public comment missed in the first quarter of 2026/27, reported 2026-10-06
position_start: Described as still before Parliament in an opinion piece (2026-05)
position_end: Not yet revised for public comment: the department's quarterly report to Parliament's home affairs committee records the first-quarter target missed, blaming delay in appointing a legal drafting provider (2026-10)
sources: 2026-10-06-problem-with-plan-for-digital-ids-in-south-africa|2026-05-29 Opinion South Africa's Digital Identity Regulations A Governance Crossroads
note: named as the statutory foundation the digital-ID regulations should rest on; the department's own report has it at revision for comment, which the earlier account of it as before Parliament does not match

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Land Transport Amendment Act and Regulations
milestone: Act gazetted 11 June 2024; the Second Regulations gazetted 12 September 2025
position_start: Did not exist as a national registration regime reaching e-hailing services
position_end: In force: the Amendment Act of 2023 gazetted in June 2024 and the Second National Land Transport Regulations of 2025 gazetted in September 2025, which together carry the national registration regime the e-hailing licence work rests on
note: The primary instruments behind the e-hailing operating-licence regime recorded separately under Technology.

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Payment System Bill
position_end: a bill the central bank governor says will soon go out for public comment, moving payment regulation from an entity-based model to an activity-based one

subject: gov.legislate
name: OECD Common Reporting Standard regulations
position_start: The standard in force on the prior regulations
position_end: Amended regulations gazetted, updating the legal and technical basis for automatic cross-border exchange of financial-account information
note: the only cross-border data-transfer instrument on this ledger with an operating exchange behind it

subject: gov.legislate
name: Online Intermediation Platforms Guidance Note
position_end: Final guidance in force for leading online intermediation platforms, naming price-parity clauses, interoperability restrictions, self-preferencing and misuse of competitively sensitive data as the competition risks the commission will act on
note: guidance rather than regulation; no enforcement action under it is on file

subject: gov.legislate
name: Operation Vulindlela reporting
position_end: "Uneven and slower than anticipated"

subject: gov.legislate
name: Operator association exemption to share infrastructure planning data
milestone: Application filed with the Competition Commission, reported 2026-09-08
position_end: The Association of Comms and Technology, whose members are Vodacom, MTN, Telkom, Cell C, Rain and Liquid, has applied to the Competition Commission for a five-year exemption under Chapter 2 of the Competition Act allowing members to share limited infrastructure planning information through an independent third party, to identify connectivity gaps, cut duplicated build and lower deployment cost where a single operator cannot justify the investment; the communications minister called the proposal encouraging for rural communities and townships
note: the application’s filing date and the Commission’s timetable are unestablished; what is held is two trade and newspaper accounts of its existence and scope, the earlier of them putting the listed majors behind it at more than R700bn of market value

subject: gov.legislate
name: POPIA amendment for artificial intelligence and privacy by design
milestone: Amendment work stated by the Information Regulator, 18 August 2026
position_end: The Information Regulator states it is working with the justice department to amend the Act to cover artificial intelligence and privacy by design; no draft, gazette notice or timetable is published
note: Stated at a webinar alongside the rights commission, which framed data breaches as a constitutional harm.

subject: gov.legislate
name: POPIA enforcement notices
position_end: Fines followed notices in October 2026: an R1 million infringement notice and an enforcement notice, signed 2026-10-21, to First National Bank over a 2022 compromise exposing 88 data subjects' information, and R500,000 on a Johannesburg TVET college for not complying with a 22 May 2026 enforcement notice; in August the national bureau of standards received a notice over its 2024 ransomware attack

subject: gov.legislate
name: Position on age assurance for under-16s
position_start: Not previously held by this repository
position_end: The government is not pursuing any blanket policy restricting under-16s from social media, the communications and digital technologies minister told parliament in a written answer reported 10 September 2026, saying platforms should instead strengthen their own protections against harmful content. The position separates the country from a growing number of states, several of them African, considering or adopting age-assurance requirements.
note: the department states the position directly: no legislation is planned, the minister citing no irrefutable indication that a general access ban keeps under-16s off the platforms and emerging evidence of bans being bypassed; still a stated position rather than an instrument, and no review, consultation or alternative measure is named

subject: gov.legislate
name: Public Administration Management Act 11 of 2014
position_end: In force as the statutory frame for administration-wide arrangements across national, provincial and municipal spheres, including the transfer and secondment of employees and the establishment of common norms and standards
note: the standing statute under which administration-wide standards such as the Digital Public Services Standard are authorised

subject: gov.legislate
name: Regulator's power to condone a late licence renewal
milestone: Constitutional Court approached after two losses on the point
position_start: Assumed by the regulator and untested
position_end: Lost in the High Court and the Supreme Court of Appeal to a community radio station that filed two weeks late, and taken to the Constitutional Court (2026-09)
note: The regulator argues the Electronic Communications Act leaves it the discretion; two courts have read it otherwise.

subject: gov.legislate
name: SADC real-time settlement
position_end: Kwanza added 2026-07-27

subject: gov.legislate
name: Statistics Act 6 of 1999 and Statistics Amendment Act 29 of 2024
position_start: The 1999 Act in force, the 2024 Amendment Act assented and not proclaimed
position_end: The Amendment Act proclaimed for implementation and implementation reported as progressing, with regulations and twenty memoranda of understanding under development to carry it
note: the proclamation date itself is not stated in the held account, only that proclamation had occurred

subject: gov.protect
name: Consumer Protection Act direct-marketing opt-out registry
position_start: Regulations shifting the anti-spam duty to the National Consumer Commission (2026-04)
position_end: The National Consumer Commission issued a request for proposals for service providers to augment the national opt-out registry system, aiming to have it live in 2026; direct marketers must register and cleanse lists against it, a consumer's pre-emptive block overrides prior consent, and fines reach R1m or 10% of annual turnover; the commission launched the registry on 7 October 2026: direct marketers register from 15 September to December 2026 and cleanse their lists from December 2026, and consumers register pre-emptive blocks from May 2027; draft compliance guidelines were gazetted for comment on 2 October 2026
note: the request's issue date and closing date are not stated

subject: gov.protect
name: Operator data retention in a two-decade compensation claim
milestone: Position maintained through the Constitutional Court
position_end: The operator's position throughout a two-decade claim over a call-back product was that the data needed to value it did not exist: it told the Constitutional Court that it retains only six months of operational data at a time and that no record links a message to any corresponding or induced return call, so both sides' valuations were modelled rather than measured, off a July 2017 data-mining exercise covering six months of messages, six months of call-data records and prepaid records showing zero-airtime balances. Courts had twice ordered production, in 2011 for all product call records from 2000 and in June 2020 for data and financial information; 2016 court documents record that the operator's then financial director had proposed tracking the product
note: a retention practice tested in litigation rather than by a regulator, and the clearest published statement of what an operator does and does not keep

subject: gov.protect
name: Police body-worn cameras with facial recognition
position_end: Body-worn cameras for the police service must be able to conduct facial recognition, according to state IT agency tender documents published in the week to 10 September 2026. The requirement sits in the bid specification for RFB 3286-2026, a three-year contract for the supply, delivery, support and maintenance of body-worn and vehicle dashboard cameras and related software, whose scope says the solution must give the police the ability to conduct facial recognition and to integrate with various security platforms. Bids close at 11am on 29 September 2026.
note: a bid specification, not an award: no contract value, camera volume, matching database, retention period, authorising legal instrument or data-protection assessment is published, and the personal information regulator's position on it is not held

subject: gov.protect
name: POPIA Regulations on the processing of data subjects' health information
milestone: Gazetted 54268 and effective on publication, 6 March 2026
position_end: Final regulations under POPIA governing the processing of data subjects' health information by certain responsible parties, effective on publication and binding on confidentiality, integrity, availability and cross-border transfer
note: Subordinate legislation under the Act, not an amendment to it.

subject: gov.protect
name: Protection of Personal Information Act and Information Regulator
milestone: Regulator names the compliance grace period as the Act's key weakness
movement: No change, the regulator states the gap itself
position_end: In force with enforcement powers since July 2021, and the regulator's chair states the compliance grace period is the Act's key weakness because a body that complies in time cannot then be fined; the Regulator also states it has no capability to test external systems for privacy compliance before launch
note: the regulator's chairperson names consent, retention and transparency management and the absence of a national artificial-intelligence policy as the complexities it now works against, and says the regulator is not convinced that privacy by default or personal information impact assessments are being practised; its POPIA executive adds that models retaining personal information beyond its purpose contradicts the Act. An adequacy model rather than hard localisation - cross-border transfers permitted where equivalent protection, consent or contractual necessity applies under s.72, with the controller accountable under s.19

subject: gov.protect
name: Publication of school-leaving results in the press under POPIA
milestone: Regulator's appeal lodged at the Supreme Court of Appeal, August 2026
position_start: Results published as exam numbers only, surnames dropped in 2014, with three regulator challenges dismissed in the Pretoria High Court
position_end: The regulator has taken the challenge to the Supreme Court of Appeal, arguing the basic education department is obliged to release results directly to learners and has no contract or legal basis for press publication, and that sequentially issued exam numbers still leave matriculants identifiable - a contention the High Court dismissed as fanciful and unsupported by empirical evidence; the case traces to a November 2023 POPIA assessment and a notice not to publish the 2024 results
note: The newspaper publisher is a respondent and has not opposed.

subject: gov.regional
name: Africa Semiconductor Technical Advisory Group (ASTAG)
position_end: A continental advisory group launched by AUDA-NEPAD with the CSIR, the African Academy of Sciences and the science department, charged with a refined Africa Semiconductor Roadmap for 2026-2030, a map of continental capability and frameworks for pooled regional infrastructure within twelve months
note: no funding, host secretariat or membership list published

subject: gov.regional
name: Regional higher education data system (SADC)
milestone: Named an immediate priority at the regional vice-chancellors' meeting, 31 August 2026
position_end: Agreement on a regional higher education data system was set as one of five immediate priorities at a regional vice-chancellors' strategic meeting in Johannesburg on 31 August 2026, alongside implementation priorities for the regional higher education strategy, a network model for a proposed regional university, better qualifications recognition and credit transfer, and flagship research and skills programmes. The higher education minister set the test as students and academics having moved and data being shared by the June 2027 meeting of regional education, science and technology ministers, rather than documents completed
note: a priority, not an instrument: no design, host, funding or data scope is stated, and the June 2027 test is the only date on it

subject: gov.standards
name: AI-in-finance regulatory framework
note: the Prudential Authority's 2025/26 report embeds AI, cloud, cyber and data-offshoring into bank supervision and ran a first nationwide AI-adoption survey, naming regulatory uncertainty, AI skills and governance as the barriers

subject: gov.standards
name: Biometric and cryptographic standards revision
position_start: Did not exist on the repository
position_end: Drafts out for comment on biometric performance testing, biometric information protection and cryptographic module testing, revising the biometric interface and identification-card standards and proposing one service-management standard for withdrawal
note: the standards that would govern the biometric systems reported elsewhere in this document are being revised while those systems are already in service

subject: gov.standards
name: Crypto-asset service provider licensing
milestone: Regulator states the licensing model does not reach decentralised finance, 11 August 2026
position_end: Licensing of centralised crypto-asset service providers is in force, but the regulator states the model has no purchase on decentralised finance - protocols with no company, board or natural person to hold accountable - and plans to attach obligations elsewhere; no instrument for DeFi is published
note: 300 licences by end-2025 on the earlier source's figure; the FSCA had licensed 310 crypto asset service providers by 2026-03-31, a figure carried in the Reserve Bank's Financial Stability Review

subject: gov.standards
name: Digital health conformance testing laboratory
milestone: First formal testing event set for 26-28 January 2026
position_end: A laboratory being set up with the CSIR to test patient information systems against the gazetted interoperability standards, with a first formal testing event set for January 2026
note: no result of the January event is held

subject: gov.standards
name: Digital Public Services Standard
position_end: In force as a national lifecycle and quality baseline for digital public services, covering accessibility, security, ethics, testing and quality assurance, deployment and retirement
note: no compliance report, assessment or departmental adoption count has been published against it

subject: gov.standards
name: ICT and Media Regulators Forum
note: Parliament's communications committee prefers strengthening ICASA, the Information Regulator, the Competition Commission and the National Consumer Commission through this forum to creating the four AI bodies the withdrawn draft policy proposed

subject: gov.standards
name: SABS draft AI standards (ISO/IEC adoptions)
position_end: The national standards body published drafts adopting ISO/IEC AI standards unmodified, on transparency, data quality and human oversight, for comment to 10 November 2026
note: a law firm's explainer; the drafts themselves are not held

subject: gov.standards
name: SABS participation in ISO/IEC JTC 1
position_end: The national standards body is a participating member of the joint ISO/IEC information technology committee and its subcommittees on security, identification cards, biometrics, AI and IT governance

subject: gov.discourse
name: Harmful online content governance review
position_end: Finds the statutory framework adequate but its governance fragmented, and content moderation conducted in English to the exclusion of ten official languages
note: The language finding is the operative one: the law reaches speech the moderation does not read

subject: gov.discourse
name: Policy brief on information integrity and human rights
milestone: Launched at a rights commission stakeholder engagement 2026-08-19
position_end: Published by the rights commission, and launched with a deputy justice minister's statement that government should not become the custodian of truth on disinformation while the information environment should not be left to private platforms' algorithms, grounded in sections 16, 19 and 32 of the Constitution
note: a policy brief rather than an instrument; no legislative proposal or timetable follows from it on the record

subject: finance.budget
name: Universal Service and Access Fund collections and unspent balance
milestone: About R652m unspent at the end of 2025/26
position_end: The regulator collected R1.29bn for the fund over 2021/22 to 2025/26 and about R652m was unspent at the end of 2025/26, on the minister's reply to Parliament, which blames delays in set-top-box installation and in broadband projects

subject: finance.mou
name: MzansiXchange partner institutions
position_end: Eleven institutions named as joint partners in the national data exchange pilot at its launch, the standing set of relationships underpinning it
note: no memorandum text, term or financial commitment is published for any of the eleven

subject: finance.new
name: Compliance platform investment (Instarc)
position_end: A EUR 1.25 million strategic investment to commercialise a cloud compliance platform for accountable institutions under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act (2026-09)

subject: finance.new
name: G20 and digital public infrastructure roadmap support (Gates Foundation)
position_end: A US$1.1m Gates Foundation grant, fully disbursed, to the consultancy Genesis Analytics for technical support to the government in developing digital public infrastructure to improve vulnerable people's access to services
note: Paid to a private consultancy, not to government; no roadmap text is held

subject: finance.new
name: Global business services centre investment (Cape Town)
milestone: Centre opened on a R70 million investment
position_end: An artificial-intelligence customer-experience and business-process firm opened a global business services centre in the Cape Town central business district on a R70 million investment, taking its South African workforce from about 1,500 to 2,100. The company has grown from a 50-person operation in 2022 and has trained more than 350 learners through its own academy, which recruits from disadvantaged and high-risk communities
note: the date of the R70 million commitment is not established; the source dates only its own publication

subject: finance.new
name: IFC financing for WIOCC and its South African data-centre property company
position_end: A sustainability-linked loan of up to US$20.8 million, in dollars to the group's Mauritius operator and in rand to its South African data-centre property company, approved on 5 December 2025 and invested on 14 May 2026, reported alongside up to US$50 million of IFC equity in a US$577 million expansion plan
note: the lender's disclosure gives up to US$20.8 million and a press account US$20.4 million; the equity figure and the expansion plan are the press account's; a separate US$15 million local-currency loan from Ninety One to the data-centre subsidiary, for a new South African facility, was announced on 15 December 2025

subject: finance.new
name: Moment Series A round
position_end: A US$22m Series A for a pan-African payments-infrastructure firm, led by AlphaCode Venture Partners with General Catalyst, MultiChoice and Canal+, taking its total raised to US$55m
note: the per-investor split is not disclosed

subject: finance.new
name: Recapitalisation of the Vivica fibre and telecoms group
milestone: French development financier put in US$20m through a private-equity-led consortium, 2026-10-05
position_end: New shares subscribed across Frogfoot, Vox and Hypa at a combined after-debt equity value of R8.4bn, with the rollout to reach 360,000 connected homes a year within 12 months. The lead investor has since put its commitment at more than R2.1bn across the fibre group and two digital-services firms, its consortium holding 34.8% of the fibre companies at an aggregate R14.4bn valuation, with the fibre growth capital aimed at 360,000 township and lower-income homes over 12 months; a French development finance institution said on 5 October 2026 that it is investing US$20m in the fibre operator and its two service providers through a consortium managed by a private equity firm, with British, Belgian and German development financiers and three South African investors, aimed at fibre in lower-income and township areas
note: the subscription amount is not disclosed - the R8.4bn is the implied equity value of the companies, not the money raised; the stated targets are the parties' own

subject: finance.new
name: Science and Technology Accelerator-Systems, Southern Africa
milestone: Expressions of interest opened, deadline extended to 26 August 2026
position_end: Up to GBP2.5m over three years to March 2030, of which up to GBP400,000 for 2026/27, covering artificial intelligence and emerging technologies and digital access alongside climate, energy, health and space; South Africa the primary focus, Zimbabwe and Zambia the first year's
note: at expressions-of-interest stage: the fund is resourced but the delivery consortium is not chosen, and contract signature is expected within 2026

subject: finance.new
name: Township enterprise digital and data backbone
milestone: US$1,000,000 committed to scale the platform
position_end: A United Nations development agency committed US$1,000,000 to scale a digital and data backbone for township micro, small and medium enterprises
note: a commitment record rather than a delivery report; no enterprise count, coverage or disbursement is stated

subject: finance.new
name: United States development finance equity in a Johannesburg-headquartered operator
milestone: Board announcement of 16 September 2026, amount unpublished
position_end: The United States development finance corporation's board approved an equity investment in a Johannesburg-headquartered operator of undersea cables, fibre networks and data centres in more than 30 African countries, naming two investment partners. The board announcement published no amount; one press account puts it at around R2.5 billion, up to US$155 million, as a ceiling rather than a committed sum
note: the figure is a news organisation's and not the investor's; no disbursement schedule, stake or conditions are published

subject: finance.new
name: US development finance loan to Africa Data Centres
milestone: Credited with a 6MW Cape Town expansion, live 2024-07-25
position_end: Up to US$300 million in direct loans within a US$428.6 million project, lent to a UK-registered holding company to acquire and expand data centres in South Africa and Kenya and to enter other African markets; the operator credits it with a three-hall, 6MW expansion of its first Cape Town facility, live in July 2024
note: the 2020 summary states a proposed loan; the operator's release does not state an amount drawn

subject: infra.connect
name: 2Africa West subsea route
position_end: Open for business with South African landings at Yzerfontein and Duynefontein, an in-window addition to international bandwidth capacity
note: no capacity, price or utilisation figure is published for the landings

subject: infra.connect
name: Analogue television switch-off date
milestone: No date set; R567m of digital-migration inventory written off in 2025/26
position_end: No analogue switch-off date has been set, pending a steering committee of broadcasters and stakeholders; 52,869 of the households registered for subsidised set-top boxes still cannot be located, down from about 80,000 at the previous meeting, and a data-cleaning exercise cut the installation target from 447,815 to 401,803 households against which 290,506 installations are complete and verified; the minister's reply to Parliament of 30 September 2026 records a R567m write-off of digital-migration inventory in 2025/26
note: the communications department told parliament no date has been set, sixteen years past the original 2010 deadline; estimates of households still dependent on analogue range from about 500,000 on one civil-society account to between 2.2m and 4.5m on two others, and the record reconciles none of them

subject: infra.connect
name: Broadband Infraco cross-border backhaul
position_end: The state wholesaler reaches the borders of all six land neighbours and acts as their gateway to international capacity, upgrading its Botswana route with added redundancy (2019-07)
note: the company's own account; the planned merger with the state signal distributor is a separate row

subject: infra.connect
name: Broadcasting Digital Migration programme
status: In development, analogue switch-off suspended and before the courts
milestone: Parliamentary committee to reconvene within three months, stated 2026-10-06
position_end: Begun in 2008 against a switch-off deadline of 1 November 2011; the analogue switch-off suspended and before the courts for the second time, with dual-illumination costs continuing (2026-10)
note: the set-top box subsidy was projected at ZAR5-6bn against ZAR2.5bn held from the Treasury in March 2013

subject: infra.connect
name: Cape Town internet exchange (CINX)
milestone: Two further data-centre sites live, 3 August 2026
position_end: Present at six data-centre locations after going live at two further sites, but still concentrated: one facility holds 87 of the exchange's 122 networks and nearly every 100 Gbps port, against 208 networks and 10,132 Gbps on the more distributed Johannesburg exchange
note: Distribution across sites is not the same as resilience while one facility carries most of the peering.

subject: infra.connect
name: Cell C 5G service
milestone: Went live for customers without a launch event, 2026-08-21
position_end: The third mobile operator's 5G service live for customers, claimed as the widest 5G coverage in the country because it roams on all of both larger operators' 5G sites at 2.6GHz and 3.5GHz rather than owning radio infrastructure
note: national coverage here is a contractual asset rather than a capital one; the launch carried no event and no mention in the company's maiden full-year results

subject: infra.connect
name: Data-centre incentive instrument (SEZ, depreciation, grid priority)

subject: infra.connect
name: Digital Connectivity Investment Roadmap to 2035
position_end: A development bank and planning commission study costing universal, meaningful broadband access against the 2030 development plan, the national broadband programme and the 2050 infrastructure plan: connecting every household needs about R140bn under least-cost deployment and well above R200bn under fibre-led scenarios, or R108bn to R142bn in 2025 real terms depending on the economic scenario. It is built on a 0.76 square-kilometre hexagonal-grid geospatial mapping exercise and a lender infrastructure-investment framework, and its data-centre annex puts the country at nearly 500MW of potential critical IT capacity (2026-09)
note: a costed roadmap, not a funded programme: no appropriation, delivery vehicle or commencement is attached to any scenario

subject: infra.connect
name: Draft Radio Frequency Spectrum and Fees Regulations amendments
position_end: Gazetted 2026-05-15; oral hearings 19-20 August 2026
note: draft amendments to the Radio Frequency Spectrum Regulations 2015 and the Radio Frequency Spectrum Fees Regulations 2010, both published in Government Gazette No. 54677 on 2026-05-15; ICASA lists five areas - a registration regime for satellite space segment operators, revised spectrum fee formulas, blanket licensing for satellite terminal networks, protection of radio astronomy facilities and rules for Earth Stations in Motion; hybrid oral hearings at Centurion on 19 and 20 August 2026, confined to stakeholders who filed written comments

subject: infra.connect
name: Equiano submarine cable
milestone: Wholesale service live 2023-03-15, after landing at Melkbosstrand in August 2022
position_end: Landed at Melkbosstrand in August 2022: about 15,000 km from Portugal with 12 fibre pairs and a design capacity of 144 Tbps, carrying a Cape Town to Lisbon wholesale route from March 2023
note: design figures as given in an operator's launch account; no lit-capacity or utilisation figure held

subject: infra.connect
name: Equinix Cape Town land use
milestone: Appeal before the Planning Appeals Advisory Panel 2026-10-12; mayoral decision due within 90 days
position_end: The municipal planning tribunal's 14 July 2026 rezoning, subdivision and consolidation approval for a hyperscale data centre at King Air Industria is under formal appeal by the Housing Assembly and Foxglove, represented by the Legal Resources Centre, who say nearby communities were not properly consulted and that the application lacked information on electricity, water, emissions and noise impacts. The tribunal's decision created a new "data centre" land-use category
note: the city confirms the July rezoning is suspended and cannot be acted on until the appeal is finalised, with the appeal report going to the executive mayor as planning appeals authority; the operator calls the site a long-term land bank, says it has no immediate plans to develop it and has submitted no planning or development application; no appeal timetable is published; the panel date and the 90-day period for the mayor's decision are on an appellant's own published account, which puts the approved land rights at up to 174MVA

subject: infra.connect
name: Gauteng SMART Schools Programme
milestone: Legislature oversight visits to schools began 17 September 2026
note: the provincial legislature's e-government committee began oversight visits to schools after engagements in which it identified concerns about ICT infrastructure reliability, network capacity and maintenance; no school count, budget, device figure or connectivity measure is published

subject: infra.connect
name: Government network site speeds
milestone: Auditor-General's briefing on the 2025/26 audits, reported 2026-10-11
movement: No change, a first count with no earlier figure behind it
position_end: 2,076 of about 7,800 sites on the state IT agency's network ran below 10Mbps and 294 government facilities were still on legacy copper, on the Auditor-General's 2025/26 audit briefing; the broadband programme added about 8,000 connections and 1,000 upgrades against a 14,742-site target for the year
note: the figures are reported from the Auditor-General's briefing to Parliament; the briefing document itself is not held

subject: infra.connect
name: High-demand spectrum auction
milestone: Release quantified by the 2026 National Radio Frequency Plan
position_end: The 2026 National Radio Frequency Plan targets 1,145 MHz more mid-band spectrum and over 17,250 MHz of mmWave against 794 MHz currently available - roughly 215% more high-demand spectrum cleared for release - but no auction has been scheduled, priced or gazetted

subject: infra.connect
name: IMT Roadmap 2026 and draft assignment plans
position_end: Out for consultation
note: 794 MHz assigned today against 19 625 MHz identified and 18 831 MHz to be assigned, 17 250 MHz of it mmWave with none assigned; the roadmap reaches to IMT-2030; the 850 MHz, 18 588 MHz and 215% figures in circulation are ICASA's media statement and appear nowhere in the instrument

subject: infra.connect
name: LEO satellite licensing framework
milestone: Draft satellite licensing framework stated as developed, reported 2026-10-08
position_end: Direction rejected 2026-05; the minister publicly backs LEO entry while conceding licensing is the regulator's alone, and the 30% equity requirement stands; the regulator's chairperson said, reported 8 October 2026, that the authority has developed a draft satellite licensing framework; the draft is not published
note: the operator asked how the 30% historically-disadvantaged equity requirement in the spectrum regulations applies to the new gateway and user-terminal licence categories, which the draft does not say

subject: infra.connect
name: METISS submarine cable
position_end: A 3,200km, 24 Tbps cable linking Mauritius, Reunion and Madagascar to a landing near Durban, built by a six-operator Indian Ocean consortium and in service since 5 March 2021
note: no South African operator is among the six consortium members

subject: infra.connect
name: Mombasa to Johannesburg terrestrial fibre route
position_end: A terrestrial-only fibre route from Mombasa to Johannesburg through the DRC, including a Goma to Kananga link, launched by a private pan-African group as an alternative to east-coast subsea cables
note: the operator's own announcement; no capacity is stated

subject: infra.connect
name: MTN acquisition of IHS Holding
position_end: The Competition Commission recommended that the Tribunal approve the operator group's acquisition of the tower company, on conditions: fair and non-discriminatory access to its towers for every operator with no preference for MTN SA, fair renewal of existing leases, protection of customers' competitively sensitive information and an operationally independent tower company, plus protection of jobs and historically disadvantaged ownership
note: the Tribunal had not ruled at 2026-09-30; the tower count in South Africa is not stated

subject: infra.connect
name: National broadband map (DBSA)
position_end: Launched 2026-03-31
sources: 2026-03-31 SA finally has a broadband map - and it reveals where the gaps are

subject: infra.connect
name: National CSIRT (Cybersecurity Hub)
position_end: Operating; no incident statistics published
note: set up in 2015 by the then Department of Telecommunications and Postal Services under the National Cybersecurity Policy Framework; it coordinates and routes reports to a sector CSIRT or the SAPS rather than resolving them, states it has no control over investigation and resolution, and operates 08:00-16:30 on weekdays with no published out-of-hours capability; as at 2026-08-04 it published no incident statistics, advisories archive, annual or quarterly report and no data downloads

subject: infra.connect
name: National cyber-security measurement
position_end: Unchanged; no re-measurement

subject: infra.connect
name: National Cybersecurity Policy Framework
position_end: In force; the instrument the national CSIRT rests on
note: approved by Cabinet in March 2012 and named by the Cybersecurity Hub as the mandate under which it operates as the national CSIRT; established from the Hub's own site on 2026-08-04, and the framework's own text is not held

subject: infra.connect
name: National GIS infrastructure database (rapid deployment reg. 7)
milestone: Directed by ministerial policy direction gazetted 2026-10-20
position_end: A national GIS database of communications infrastructure directed by the minister's policy direction of 20 October 2026, after Icasa's draft of April 2026
sources: 2026-10-20-zaf-dcdt-policy-direction-icasa-network-deployment-facilities-leasing|2026-04-12 Icasa moves to mandate national infrastructure database
note: draft regulation 7 would compel every licensed operator to submit geo-referenced data on all passive infrastructure plus roll-out plans bi-annually to prescribed standards, with fines up to R1m

subject: infra.connect
name: National Radio Frequency Plan 2026
position_end: Gazetted 2026-07-24
note: re-bases the 8.3 kHz - 3 000 GHz allocation table on the ITU Radio Regulations 2024, keeps South Africa in ITU Region 1 with national variations only under RR 4.4, and aligns to AfriSAP and the SADC Frequency Allocation Plan; ministerial approval 2026-07-02, gazetted GN 4044 in GG 55046

subject: infra.connect
name: National wholesale 5G home-broadband network
milestone: Wholesale sales opened 2026-08; first ISP live September 2026
position_end: Selling wholesale, 5G-core only, with the first retail ISP due live in September 2026
note: a privately-financed network sold only at wholesale, with ISPs and MVNOs setting their own pricing and owning the customer relationship; the chief executive accepted the description that this is the wholesale open-access network the state spent more than a decade trying to licence and abandoned. Funded by a multibillion-rand raise after Nedbank Private Equity's December exit, with Platform Investment Partners the largest single shareholder, Wimsey Capital second, Convergence Partners and Solcon Capital continuing and RMB providing debt. No coverage footprint, site count, capacity or wholesale price is published, so what has entered service cannot be sized

subject: infra.connect
name: Policy direction on network deployment and facilities leasing, 2026
position_end: Directs Icasa to review the 2010 Facilities Leasing Regulations, develop Rapid Deployment Regulations, build a national GIS database of communications infrastructure and set up a process for disputes between operators and landowners, prevailing over the 2023 rapid-deployment policy where they differ

subject: infra.connect
name: Policy direction reserving high-demand spectrum for a wireless open access network (2019)
position_start: In force since 2019, the network never licensed
position_end: The minister withdrew the requirement that certain high-demand spectrum be reserved first for a wireless open access network, finalising a withdrawal published in draft in March 2022, so that the spectrum is available for the regulator to licence; wholesale, universal-service, anti-concentration and empowerment obligations on licensees are retained, as is the 2024 set-aside for the State Digital Infrastructure Company

subject: infra.connect
name: Public service institutions connected under the 2022 spectrum-licence obligations
milestone: Regulator's figures to Parliament's communications committee, 2026-10-14
position_end: 10,851 of 21,878 targeted public service institutions connected (49.1%) as at March 2026, with two operators below the 65% minimum threshold
note: the regulator's own count

subject: infra.connect
name: Radio frequency spectrum fees regulations for satellite
milestone: Draft amendment published 2026-05; operator representations filed 2026-06-29
position_end: Draft amendment under consultation, with the largest prospective entrant asking for flat per-licence fees and a ten-year minimum term
note: the representations of 2026-06-29 on the regulator's Draft Amendment of the Radio Frequency Spectrum Fees Regulations are now held first-hand, in the redacted copy the regulator published: they ask for a flat annual licence fee rather than bandwidth-based pricing, charging per licence rather than per earth-station site, blanket licensing for terminal networks including earth stations in motion, a frequency-factor table extended beyond 50 GHz, and a ten-year minimum licence duration; the submission also asks the regulator for consolidated guidance on local-entity requirements, the 30% historically-disadvantaged-group equity threshold and the ICT Sector Code, which ties the fee consultation to the ownership question the licensing framework is already stuck on

subject: infra.connect
name: Réunion to South Africa submarine cable
position_end: A EUR93 million consortium led by La Reunion Connectee, joined by Free through Telco OI, to build a 16-fibre-pair submarine cable linking La Reunion directly to South Africa, planned for service in 2028 as the successor route to SAFE, in service since 2002 and at end of life
note: no commitment is attributed to a single financier, so no deal record was built

subject: infra.connect
name: SA Connect phase 2
milestone: Completion-year position in the Budget Review
position_end: Reached its 2025/26 completion year with about 1,180 km of fibre, roughly 5.6 million households reached through community wireless access and 6,343 government facilities connected

subject: infra.connect
name: Satellite market entry via section 13
position_end: Amazon Leo–Herotel, 2026-07-15; the satellite operator said on 7 October 2026 that it has applied for licences for a direct-to-device service, working with mobile operators and probably from around 2028, beside the fixed service its distributor is to sell from 2027

subject: infra.connect
name: SEACOM submarine cable
milestone: One-off repair costs reported in a shareholder's results, 2025-03-25
position_end: In service since 2009 on a 17,000 km route linking South Africa with Mozambique, Tanzania, Kenya, Djibouti, France and India; breaks in the Red Sea and a fault off Mtunzini drove repair costs that cut its contribution to a 30% shareholder's headline earnings to R2m from R32m in the half to December 2024

subject: infra.connect
name: Sector coverage and household internet access
position_end: Fourth-generation population coverage at 99.5% and fifth-generation at 58.0%, household internet access at 82.1% and fixed internet at home at 17.4%, with 4,377 of 21,878 government facilities connected as at October 2025
note: the regulator's own annual measurement; the 2025 edition is held as the prior and its figures are not restated here

subject: infra.connect
name: State Digital Infrastructure Company (network merger)
position_end: Implementation moved to FY2028/29
sources: 2026-04-28 State broadband merger limps into a second decade

subject: infra.connect
name: State signal distributor financial position
position_start: A net loss after tax of R246 million in 2024/25, driven primarily by a provision for expected credit loss reflecting customers' economic difficulties
position_end: A net loss after tax of R60 million in 2025/26, an improvement of about 76%, alongside a clean audit outcome with no material findings and achievement of 90% against predetermined objectives.
note: still loss-making; the entity's own reported results, with no revenue figure, customer-debt recovery or analogue-switch-off cost attribution held against them

subject: infra.connect
name: Sustainable Connectivity and Community-Led Digital Economies in South Africa Project
milestone: Launched at Inanda 2026-08-25; R7m programme and targets published 2026-09-15
position_end: A R7m UK-funded programme, run with the communications department, supporting 25 local community network operators in KwaZulu-Natal to deploy 250 public Wi-Fi hotspots, connect 150 public facilities and reach 1,500 homes, on a shared wireless open-access model, with a cable company and a technology credit fund providing infrastructure and finance (2026-09)
note: targets, not delivered counts; no term or completion date is stated, and the national wireless open-access network the model borrows from is on hold

subject: infra.connect
name: Swiftnet tower portfolio ownership
milestone: Sale by the incumbent operator completed 2025-03-28
position_end: More than 4,000 tower sites sold by Telkom for an enterprise value of about R6.75 billion to a consortium in which an Actis-led group including the Mineworkers Investment Company holds 70% and Royal Bafokeng Holdings 30%
note: Telkom remains an anchor tenant

subject: infra.connect
name: Third national fibre route, Cape Town to Pretoria
position_start: Two long-haul routes, a double break on which isolated much of the country in 2025
position_end: A third Cape Town to Pretoria route completed via Springbok and Mahikeng, built so the network stays up through major breaks, within a wholesale fibre network of about 180,000km carrying just under R3bn of capital expenditure a year (2026-09)
note: no capacity, commissioning date or route-diversity measure is published for the new path

subject: infra.connect
name: Umoja fibre route
position_end: A route from Kenya through five countries to South Africa and the Johannesburg cloud region, its terrestrial path built with a private carrier, before an Indian Ocean crossing to Australia still to be laid (2024-05)
note: no completion date for the ocean segment is given

subject: infra.connect
name: Upper 6GHz 5G-Advanced trial
milestone: Trial completed under a temporary radio licence, stated 2026-10-13
position_end: An operator completed a 5G-Advanced trial in the upper 6GHz band under a temporary licence, reaching 10.35 Gbps peak downloads on 400 MHz; the band, allocated in full to mobile in the 2026 frequency plan, is not yet licensed commercially

subject: infra.connect
name: Vodacom Mpumalanga network investment
milestone: More than R600m in the current financial year, announced 2026-10-20
position_end: More than R600m in the current financial year after R620m in 2025/26; 1,408 sites, up from just over 1,300, with 45% fibre-connected, up from 41%, across all 17 local municipalities

subject: infra.connect
name: Vodacom Western Cape network investment
milestone: More than R500m in the current financial year, announced 2026-10-06
position_end: More than R500m in the current financial year, about R380m of it on modernising the radio network at more than 50 sites, with 700MHz 4G capacity upgrades at more than 50 sites, new 5G sites and backup power, in townships the operator names

subject: infra.store
name: Africa Data Centres South Africa ownership
milestone: Joint control by a domestic infrastructure fund approved by the Competition Tribunal, 4 February 2026
position_start: Wholly owned by a pan-African technology group
position_end: A domestic asset manager's infrastructure fund was cleared unconditionally to take joint control of the South African data-centre business, with a path to sole control; the parent describes the stake sold as a minority one and applies the proceeds to reducing its telecoms subsidiary's debt
note: the stake size and price are not published

subject: infra.store
name: AWS Africa (Cape Town) Region
position_start: Operating since 22 April 2020 with three availability zones, the operator's first region in Africa
position_end: The Cape Town cloud region now carries 154 services on the operator's own account, given at a Johannesburg summit on 10 September 2026, alongside a stated more than US$819 million invested in African infrastructure since 2018 and a further US$1.5 billion committed to 2029
note: every figure is the company's own; no commitment date is stated for the US$1.5 billion

subject: infra.store
name: Cape Town development guidelines for large data-centre applications
milestone: Drafting confirmed by the City, 17 September 2026; no draft published
note: the city's first public acknowledgement that its approvals process for large data-centre applications needs changing; the guidelines are being drafted and no draft, consultation timetable or adoption date is published

subject: infra.store
name: Coega artificial-intelligence data-centre campus
milestone: Direct grid connection approved by council, 27 August 2026
position_start: A proposal with no grid connection agreed
position_end: A metropolitan council approved the developer request to connect a proposed hyperscale campus at the special economic zone directly to the national utility rather than the municipal grid, for up to 556 MW, against a R3bn municipal and community infrastructure investment offered by the developer and objections from councillors
note: the connection is approved; the campus itself has no stated capacity in service, construction date or completion date

subject: infra.store
name: Continent 8 data centre, Johannesburg
position_end: A hosting and cloud provider for online gaming and betting announced its first African data centre, in Johannesburg, on 30 September 2026; the site, its capacity and any colocation partner are not disclosed

subject: infra.store
name: Data-centre foreign direct investment since 2020
position_start: Not held: the review states a cumulative figure from 2020 and no annual series
position_end: More than US$5 billion attracted since 2020, the same order as Nigeria and the largest on the continent alongside it; Africa drew more data-centre FDI projects than Emerging Europe, with African firms investing primarily within the region
note: a cumulative announced-investment figure compiled by the reviewer, not a balance-of-payments statistic; the same review names chronic load shedding as the constraint that deters the stable demand next-generation AI infrastructure requires

subject: infra.store
name: Development bank managed disaster-recovery service
position_end: A five-year managed service invited for information and communications technology backup, restore, disaster recovery, replication and business continuity
note: held as a procurement notice, so it establishes an intention to buy rather than a capability in service; a second development finance institution put out a server and storage upgrade proposal in March 2025

subject: infra.store
name: Domestic artificial-intelligence factory, global ranking
milestone: Entered the June 2026 global supercomputer list at rank 36
position_end: A domestically hosted artificial-intelligence factory ranked 36th on the June 2026 global list of the most powerful supercomputers: an HPE Cray XD670 of 285,696 cores on Xeon Platinum 8558 processors and NVIDIA H200 SXM5 141GB accelerators over InfiniBand NDR, installed in 2026 at a Cape Town data centre, measured at 77.79 PFlop/s Linpack against a theoretical peak of 102.16 PFlop/s
note: a capability ranking rather than a utilisation measure; no customer count, occupancy or workload figure is published, and the Linpack benchmark is a submitted result

subject: infra.store
name: Google Cloud Johannesburg region
position_end: Johannesburg cloud region declared operational on 31 January 2024, a year after the city was picked as the company's first African site
note: the company's own account; no capacity figure is published

subject: infra.store
name: Government Private Cloud Ecosystem (GPCE)
position_end: The state IT agency's cloud ecosystem, in production since October 2017 across hosted, on-premise government and vendor cloud variants in its data centres, with a 36-month panel being procured to migrate client applications, databases and servers onto it
note: the bid specification is the agency's own description; no capacity or migrated-workload figure is published

subject: infra.store
name: Government public cloud services across hyperscalers
milestone: 55% of the plan implemented against a 100% target, 2024/25
position_end: The state IT agency's plan to offer departments public cloud services across several hyperscalers was 55% implemented against a 100% target for 2024/25: cloud reference architectures are in place and service level agreements with the hyperscalers remain to be concluded
note: the agency's own performance report, which attributes the shortfall to the weighting of deliverables on its dashboard

subject: infra.store
name: Huawei Cloud South Africa region
position_end: Public cloud services from a tier 3+ data centre leased from a partner in Johannesburg, unveiled at AfricaCom in November 2018 and available from March 2019
note: the partner operating the leased facility is not named

subject: infra.store
name: Human rights commission inquiry into data centres
position_end: A stakeholder engagement process opened by the national human rights commission under section 184 of the Constitution and sections 13 and 18 of its own Act, to assess whether the legal, regulatory, environmental, governance and industry frameworks around data centre development meet constitutional obligations and international human rights standards. Written submissions were invited on eleven themes including electricity demand and tariffs, water use and cooling, environmental and climate impact, electronic waste, land use and community participation, data protection and privacy, transparency and accountability, and equitable access to digital infrastructure, closing 30 July 2026; the commission said in September that it had received more than 250 submissions and that the key issue emerging was the availability, consistency and transparency of information on electricity and water demand, land use, infrastructure requirements, environmental impacts and impacts on surrounding communities. The country's major operators - Equinix, Vantage, NTT Data, Africa Data Centres and Open Access Data Centres among them - answered publicly in August, defending their electricity and water use on their renewable-energy and resource-management programmes. The commission has published no finding, timetable or report date
note: civil-society groups are calling for construction of further data centres to stop until water, land and electricity use has been investigated, the municipal approval of a Cape Town hyperscale facility being the immediate trigger in a city that came close to running out of water in 2018; the president puts the country at 70 per cent of Africa's data-centre capacity, a figure given without a basis

subject: infra.store
name: JNB11 data centre ownership, Centurion
milestone: Change of control approved by the Competition Tribunal, reported 2026-09-18
position_end: Sole control of JNB11, part of a Waterfall City campus and designed for 16MW of critical IT capacity, passed from Vantage Data Centers to a buyer linked to Old Mutual's infrastructure fund manager on the tribunal's approval
note: approval date not stated; a secondary report

subject: infra.store
name: Johannesburg data-centre expansion
position_end: The operator now puts its South African build-out at about 160MW of added capacity under a R7.5bn investment programme: the Johannesburg facility opened in 2024 and scaling to 24MW, land banked in Johannesburg and Cape Town, and planning-tribunal approval won in July 2026 for two proposed Cape Town facilities expected to need about 170MW. No commitment date is stated for the programme (2026-09)
note: the capacity figures are the operator's own and mix delivered, consented and planned load; the utility separately expects a 2GW-3GW generation surplus over the next few years and names data centres among the demand it is seeking, while the human rights commission's inquiry into the sector's resource use is open

subject: infra.store
name: Microsoft cloud regions, Johannesburg and Cape Town
milestone: Third campus announced at Kosmosdal, Centurion, 2024-02-07
position_end: Cloud regions in Johannesburg and Cape Town, the first hyperscale public cloud built in the country, carrying Azure, Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 and Power Platform from November 2022, with availability zones added in 2021; a third campus at Kosmosdal, Centurion, was announced in February 2024 with no size or timeline
note: the company's own account; no capacity or occupancy figure is published

subject: infra.store
name: MTN South Africa analytics platform on Microsoft Azure (EVA 3.0)
position_end: The operator's enterprise analytics platform moved onto Microsoft Azure, processing about 22 billion records a day from more than 1,700 data feeds, and is presented as the blueprint for the group's other markets
note: where the data is hosted is not stated

subject: infra.store
name: National integrated government data centre
milestone: Proposed to the parliamentary communications committee, 24 February 2026
position_end: Proposed by the communications department as a medium- to long-term measure, operated by a repurposed state IT agency and keeping all government data in the country, with government using industry capacity in the short term; the agency now runs two national data centres, Centurion and Beta, both National Key Points, reached through 34 switching centres
note: a departmental presentation, not an adopted plan: no budget, site, capacity or date is stated; the agency tendered in 2023 for a 60-month colocation facility in Gauteng

subject: infra.store
name: OADC Isando data centre, Johannesburg
position_end: Hyperscale core facility of 12MW site load on more than 3,000 square metres of technical space, Tier III design-certified with constructed-facility certification still to come (2024-05)
note: no constructed-facility certification is held

subject: infra.store
name: Open Access Data Centres acquisition of seven facilities
position_end: Seven facilities acquired from a foreign operator on 31 December 2025 after competition approval, taking the acquirer's total capacity above 25 MW
note: a domestically headquartered operator taking over a foreign one's estate; no per-site capacity or tenancy figure is published

subject: infra.store
name: Operator artificial-intelligence data-centre venture, first phase
position_end: 150MW targeted in a first phase spanning South Africa and Nigeria, in a Gulf-backed data-centre venture in which the operator group will hold only a minority stake; the vehicle is Africa Data Hub Holding and its UAE backer was named on 27 August 2026 as Tarek Al Ashram, founder of the Dubai colocation operator Gulf Data Hub, with the operator's connectivity business a shareholder supplying open-access connectivity and go-to-market support
note: no domestic site, split of the 150MW between the two countries, cost or commissioning date is stated, and the group's own half-year results booklet of 24 August 2026 had named the vehicle but not the partner behind it

subject: infra.store
name: Oracle Cloud Johannesburg region
position_end: Region af-johannesburg-1 with one availability domain, available from 8 January 2022 and opened on 19 January 2022 as the company's first cloud region in Africa
note: the company declined to disclose the site or capacity

subject: infra.store
name: Police cloud infrastructure contract (Huawei)
milestone: Listed in the state IT agency's 2024/25 annual report, published 2025-09-29
position_end: A five-year contract for Huawei cloud infrastructure, installation, maintenance and support for the police service, awarded through the state IT agency by closed bid RFB 2736-2023 at R339,050,089
note: listed among procurements made other than by open tender; no delivery date, hosting location or data classification is stated

subject: infra.store
name: Public participation in data-centre approvals
milestone: Halt restated publicly, 2026-09-04; no participation process on record
position_end: Not held
note: civil-society groups restated the call for a halt on data-centre construction pending investigation of scarce water, land and electricity use; searched again on 2026-09-04 across the rights commission's own publications and the news record, and no participation process, commission response or moratorium is on record

subject: infra.store
name: Rights commission inquiry into data-centre expansion
