position_end: The national human rights commission is scrutinising the country's data-centre expansion, with environmental groups warning that the infrastructure required to power the state's artificial-intelligence ambitions carries costs that have not been accounted for
note: no terms of reference, hearing date or reporting deadline is published

subject: infra.store
name: Sovereign AI cloud deployment
position_end: A 7.2 EFLOPS deployment its three partners describe as Africa's most powerful AI cloud, running on more than 50 NVIDIA B300 HGX GPU servers carrying over 400 GPUs supplied through GIGABYTE's Giga Computing, in carrier-neutral Tier-3+ colocation with power supplied by the hosting partner, and pitched as keeping African AI training and inference workloads and the data behind them resident on the continent
note: the performance figure and the sovereignty framing are the partners' own announcement; no independent benchmark, customer, price or site is published

subject: infra.store
name: Standard Bank Group hybrid-cloud partnership with Huawei
milestone: Expanded partnership announced at HUAWEI CONNECT 2026, Shanghai, reported 2026-09-29
position_end: An expanded partnership, extending a 2024 agreement, to move the group's core banking systems from legacy infrastructure to a hybrid cloud platform and to work on application modernisation, data and AI, implemented in phases across a group operating in 21 African countries; no value, timetable, hosting location or data-residency terms are published
note: the account is the bank's and the supplier's own

subject: infra.store
name: Teraco and NAPAfrica ownership
milestone: Majority acquired by Digital Realty, completed 2022-08-01
position_end: Majority interest held since August 2022 by Digital Realty, a US-listed data-centre company, bought from a private-equity consortium at a valuation of about US$3.5 billion; the purchase included NAPAfrica, the continent's largest internet exchange point

subject: infra.store
name: Vodacom data platforms migration to Google Cloud
position_end: The group's critical data platforms to be migrated and unified on Google Cloud, BigQuery among them, with Gemini and Vertex AI to be applied to network, customer-care, fraud and fintech services; no timetable stated

subject: infra.store
name: Water and power constraint on the data centre pipeline
milestone: Rated relatively low on water resilience, September 2026
position_end: A ratings agency assessment puts South Africa’s water resilience as relatively low on water stress in Johannesburg, Gauteng and elsewhere, and names energy and water as the key risks to a data-centre pipeline it describes as almost twice the size of current global operating capacity across emerging markets; it says operators may need decentralised modular energy that bypasses the main grid while managing local water use, and puts the country at more than 60 known data centres with about 500MW of disclosed combined capacity (2026-09)
note: the assessment is a ratings agency’s; it lands while civil-society groups are calling for construction of further data centres to halt until the use of scarce water, land and electricity is investigated, which is recorded separately

subject: infra.energy
name: Energy availability factor
position_end: The energy availability factor at 67.55%, its highest in six years, with unplanned outages down 44.5% year on year, about 1.2 million customers removed from load reduction and 505,607 smart meters installed
note: the utility's own figures; Kusile Unit 6 entered commercial operation in September 2025, adding 800 MW and completing both flagship build programmes

subject: infra.energy
name: Household electrification and the electrification grant
position_start: Household electrification at 94.7% with 1.6 million households unelectrified, on an allocation of R3.9 billion for 2025/26
position_end: Roughly R4 billion allocated for 2026/27 against third-quarter spending of 17.6% and under-expenditure of more than R190 million, attributed to late service-provider appointments and municipal non-compliance
note: about three million households are without metered supply once illegal connections are counted; the grant is being repurposed toward universal access through micro-grid and off-grid solutions

subject: infra.energy
name: Medium-term system adequacy outlook
milestone: Assessment completed on a new method
position_end: The system operator's medium-term adequacy assessment completed on a new multi-nodal, transmission-constrained method, identifying a 2029-30 adequacy risk against an unserved-energy metric below 20 GWh
note: the first transmission-constrained adequacy assessment the repository holds; the risk it identifies falls inside the horizon of the data-centre load reported elsewhere on this ledger

subject: infra.energy
name: Strategic Framework for Offshore Wind Development
milestone: Published 10 September 2026, launched at the Africa Green Hydrogen Summit 17 September 2026
note: a framework, not an authorisation regime: it identifies about 95GW of technical potential along the coastline, 6.4GW of floating potential off Cape Town against a municipal peak of roughly 2GW and 17.4GW off Durban against about 1.7GW, and names energy-hungry coastal users including data centres as the customers that could justify building it; the laws and regulations required do not yet exist and no cost, timetable or licensing instrument is published

subject: infra.energy
name: Teraco 120MW solar plant, Free State
position_end: Construction started on a 120MW solar plant the operator owns and funds, about R2bn, its power wheeled over national and municipal networks to its data centres; operations due in 2026
note: the operator's own figures

subject: infra.capacity
name: Active .ZA domain registrations
position_end: 1.5 million active registrations across the four commercial second-level namespaces, which the registry says is a first for an African country-code domain (2026-10)
note: the registry's own count, a first measurement with no earlier figure behind it

subject: infra.capacity
name: African Compute Initiative at the University of Cape Town
milestone: Announced 2026-03-26, to be live within twelve months
position_end: A GPU-intensive AI research cluster in the university's refurbished high-performance computing data centre, under a UK-Canada AI for Development programme, described as the largest in an African higher-education institution and targeting 300 users at five or more institutions by its third year
note: the GBP 58m stated is the whole programme's, not the cluster's cost

subject: infra.capacity
name: National Integrated Cyber Infrastructure System
milestone: New 4-petaflop system delivered; phase 1 due live end-November 2026
position_start: Operating; CHPC at maximum capacity, expansion required (2026-08-05)
position_end: A new 4-petaflop system delivered and being installed in phases, the first due live by end-November 2026 and the full upgrade by end-March 2027, replacing the legacy Lengau system; NICIS ring-fenced at R292m for 2026/27
note: a Department of Science, Technology and Innovation initiative implemented by the CSIR on three pillars - the Centre for High Performance Computing, which houses the Lengau supercomputer, the South African National Research Network and the Data Intensive Research Initiative of South Africa, which operates a secure national data centre; it supports the Electronic Vaccination Data System; the Portfolio Committee on Science, Technology and Innovation reported after an oversight visit that the CHPC has reached maximum capacity and that available infrastructure is insufficient for future growth

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Bulk water utility cyber security incident
position_end: Africa's largest bulk water utility, supplying more than 16 million people across Gauteng and parts of three other provinces, disclosed a cyber security incident on 3 September 2026 in a statement to the stock exchange news service and is operating from its Centurion disaster-recovery site while it establishes the extent of the damage. Its debt officer says intruders reached some servers at night before IT staff could block them and that some servers were damaged; water treatment, water-quality control and bulk supply are stated to remain fully operational
note: a critical-infrastructure operator running from its recovery site, with no attribution, no incident class and no restoration date stated

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Commercial security operations centre, Cape Town
position_end: A 40-desk security operations centre opened in Cape Town on 14 September 2026 under a R55m investment, providing monitoring and incident response to customers in Africa and internationally, and stated to create about 100 jobs over three years. The operator entered the country by acquiring two local security businesses, in August 2024 and January 2025
note: a commercial facility: the desk count, investment figure and job number are the operator's own and no customer or public-sector mandate is stated

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cyber crime victim helpline pilot
position_end: A free, round-the-clock helpline for victims of online fraud, hacked accounts, identity theft and digital abuse, open to anyone in the country aged 13 or over, run by a local training organisation with a UK charity on funding from a US cloud provider and staffed by supervised student responders; it does not investigate or recover money but refers victims to banks, the police and mental health services, and runs an initial 12 months before any decision to expand
note: a non-state service; no caseload figure is published

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Departmental information security officer training programme
position_end: The public service and administration department is tendering to build a training programme for departmental information security officers across the public sector, to implement the directive on public service information security
note: no officer count, curriculum, budget or compliance deadline under the directive is stated

subject: infra.cybersec
name: FSCA enforcement against online financial harm
position_end: 140 public warnings; R2.89bn penalties on 76 persons (FY2025/26)
note: the FSCA's fourth Regulatory Actions Report, for 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026: most public warnings concerned unregistered providers promoting investment and trading offerings on social media and about 20% involved impersonation of licensed institutions, the FSCA and its own staff among them; the penalty jump is driven by the Banxso deepfake-advertising matter, over R2bn of the total, whose debarment and penalty reconsiderations were pending at the FSCA's report date

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Gauteng e-Panic Button app data exposure
status: Implemented, fixed; legislature committee and Information Regulator engaging the department
milestone: Department to decide on charges against the student who reported the flaw once an investigation report is in, stated 2026-10-19
position_end: The provincial e-Government department's panic-button app left its database unsecured, exposing users' names, phone numbers, crime reports (some alleging domestic violence and assault) with images and GPS coordinates, location histories back to the app's 2024 launch and one-time login PINs; the contractor fixed the flaws after a news outlet's alert of 21 September 2026, and on 29 September the department said the vulnerability had been patched and no personal information compromised, disclosing 288,307 active users, 114,414 emergency call-outs and 59,394 crimes reported since launch, an account the student who reported the flaw disputes; on 30 September the Information Regulator said it had received no security-compromise notification from the department, would engage it and could issue an information notice, and that its own recent compliance assessment of the department had not been finalised; the department put the platform contract at R269 million, with R131.3 million paid over three financial years and expiry on 10 March 2027; an opposition party said on 28 September it would report the exposure to the regulator; and on 1 October the provincial legislature's e-government committee rejected the department's assurance that no personal information was compromised and gave it seven days to report, with an incident timeline, proof of notification to the regulator and to residents, and the contract's data-protection clauses; the legislature's two committees said after a joint meeting on 5 October 2026 that the department notified the Information Regulator only that morning, about two weeks after it was alerted, could not say how many records were exposed, and that they would not accept the service provider's own investigation as independent; on 19 October 2026 the department said it would decide whether to pursue criminal charges against the student who exposed the flaw once an investigation report due the following week was in, and an opposition member of the legislature said the department had sought his prosecution
note: no count of affected users or notification to them is on record, and no report by the department to the regulator had been received at 2026-09-30

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Hungry Lion customer credential exposure
position_end: customer credentials exposed for about nine months through consumer-facing web self-service portals, on stealer-log analysis finding 23 records tied to the chain's domain, 13 of them customer accounts

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Joint Standard 2 of 2024 on cybersecurity and cyber resilience
milestone: Finalised by the financial sector regulators, reported 2025
position_end: The financial regulators' joint standard setting cybersecurity and cyber-resilience requirements for financial institutions, finalised in the 2024/25 regulation cycle

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Lengau supercomputer security breach and remediation
milestone: Cause established in a written parliamentary reply, 2026-08-19
position_end: Cause attributed to vulnerabilities in the legacy high-performance computing system, with a remediation and resilience programme since run across access controls, privileged-access management, network segmentation, patch management and monitoring, and an internal accountability review still running
note: the late-May 2026 incident at the CSIR's Centre for High Performance Computing, a pillar of the National Integrated Cyber Infrastructure System, involved unauthorised access to parts of the environment and the deployment of crypto-currency mining malware; the written reply to question NW4186 states the compromise was confined to parts of the high-performance computing environment and was not a compromise of the wider system, that ageing components are no longer fully supported by their original vendors, and that the minister declines to name individuals while due process runs. No cost, data-loss finding or outage duration is stated, and the account is the department's own

subject: infra.cybersec
name: MIP Holdings insurance-technology breach
position_end: A June 2026 extortion attack on MIP Holdings' platform exposed personal information of customers of about 45 financial-services firms; MIP reportedly paid a ransom, and by 18 September 2026 the group had turned to extorting insurers directly and dumped data allegedly from one of them on the dark web, confirmed as public by a researcher

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Payment system cybersecurity and cyber-resilience directive (Directive 1 of 2024)
milestone: Listed among the Reserve Bank's payment system directives
position_end: The Reserve Bank's directive on cybersecurity and cyber resilience within the national payment system, issued under the National Payment System Act

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Rand Mutual Assurance alleged data theft
position_end: A threat actor claims 366GB of the insurer's data, including 1.68 million compensation claims records, and demands US$95,000; the insurer says it has not established whether any information was accessed

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Ransomware attacker dwell time
position_end: 18 days in 2025 on a digital-forensics firm's own incident statistics, with some intrusions running start to finish inside a day, attributed to ransomware-as-a-service, automated reconnaissance and AI-assisted attacks
note: One firm's caseload, not a national series; a shorter dwell time is faster attack execution, not improved defence.

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Regional organised-crime operation
position_end: An eight-month international police operation against West African organised crime groups concluded with 58 arrests; no South African arrest, seizure or case figure is published
note: the country is not separately quantified in the account held, so the row records participation in a regional operation rather than a domestic outcome

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Relief grant platform security review
position_end: An external assessment commissioned after public reporting found encryption, interface and fake-website flaws in the relief grant platform; SASSA brought in biometrics and a security operations centre and shut 70 fake sites (November 2025), after a February 2025 review rated the threat medium for weak one-time-PIN login and many applicants sharing one phone

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Subscription fraud cases against telecommunications customers and operators
position_end: 14,897 subscription fraud cases in the twelve months to April 2026, a rise of 307% on the preceding year, with every month above its counterpart a year earlier; the industry body reports social engineering over messaging, calls and text overtaking technical intrusion, and AI-generated voices and messages used to make it convincing. It describes the sector as in an active systemic-risk phase in which cyberattack, fraud, infrastructure crime, energy volatility, civil unrest, regulatory pressure, climate events and supply-chain disruption amplify one another
note: a not-for-profit industry body's own report, compiled from its member operators' case records rather than a police or regulator series; the report carries no printed publication date

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Suspected breach of the eNaTIS vehicle database
milestone: Traffic infringement agency considering an investigation, reported 2026-09-18
position_end: Fake traffic-fine scams quoting motorists' correct number plates led the road traffic infringement agency to consider investigating whether the national traffic information system was accessed; the fines platform they impersonate says it was not breached, and no finding is published

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Third-party service provider breaches affecting a telecom operator, an investment platform, a bank and a financial services group
milestone: Breach reported by the provider 9 September 2026; customers notified
position_end: An unnamed provider that runs regulatory verification checks for several firms reported a breach on 9 September 2026; a telecom operator said fibre customers' names, emails, numbers and account numbers were exposed, and a bank said its data there should be treated as potentially affected pending a forensic investigation
note: a fourth name and a second supplier: a financial services group confirmed identity-related client information may have been accessed in an incident confined to its screening supplier's environment, suspended data sharing with that supplier and reinstated the service after forensic sign-off and credential replacement; the investment platform dates its own provider's disclosure to 10 September; no record count is published for any of them

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Weather Service cyberattack
milestone: Attack of 26 January 2025, reported in the 2024/25 annual report
position_end: A cyberattack on 26 January 2025 crippled the Weather Service's ICT systems and climate database and was blamed for its fall to 75% of performance targets in 2024/25

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Customs-to-customs data exchange
milestone: Roadmap and action plan adopted 26 August 2026
position_end: Customs administrations from five countries - Malawi, Mozambique, South Africa, Zambia and Zimbabwe - adopted a roadmap and action plan for customs-to-customs data exchange at a three-day meeting in Pretoria from 24 to 26 August 2026, hosted by the South African revenue service and attended by the regional secretariat. The design is to exchange trade information before consignments reach the border so that documentation and risk assessment happen earlier, phased from priority corridors, and builds on links already running between Zambia and Malawi and between Zambia and Zimbabwe
note: data standards, interoperability, cybersecurity, legal authority and information quality are all recorded as unresolved, and no corridor, date or target crossing time is named

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Digital VAT model
milestone: Statutory definitions in force 2026-04-01; consultation feedback due 2026-10-16
position_end: The VAT Act has carried the e-invoice, e-credit note, e-debit note, interoperability framework and e-reporting definitions since 1 April 2026, the statutory base for a five-corner model still out to consultation, with phased rollout from 2026/27 and feedback due 16 October 2026
note: a consultation paper rather than a rule; no cost to business, exemption threshold or accreditation regime for service providers is stated

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Home Affairs and Electoral Commission identity verification interface
milestone: Stated in place in a parliamentary reply, reported 2026-09-23
position_end: An electronic interface and system integration verifying identity details given at voter registration and voting against the National Population Register and related departmental systems, with HANIS and ABIS supplying biometric detection of duplicate, fraudulent, cancelled or blocked identity records
note: the minister's own statement in a written reply; no transaction count, rejection rate or technical specification is held

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Integrated Learner Management System
position_start: Did not exist on the repository
position_end: A shared post-school learner management platform piloting in sector education authorities, put at risk by an intellectual-property dispute and weak departmental buy-in reported to a portfolio committee
note: the dispute is over ownership of the platform rather than its function; no resolution, cost or pilot count is published

subject: dpi.exchange
name: MzansiXchange data exchange
milestone: Pilot infrastructure operational at the CSIR; pilot ends September 2026
position_end: Pilot infrastructure operational with Home Affairs, the social security agency, the student aid scheme and the public service department testing it, on a one-year pilot running October 2025 to September 2026 whose deliverables are four task teams, interoperability standards and draft data-exchange legislation
note: a year-long National Treasury pilot built on Estonia's X-Road; a federated real-time sharing rail rather than a central repository, nine months into pilot and onboarding additional technical capacity to support completion

subject: dpi.exchange
name: National health information exchange
milestone: Components in place, reported to Parliament 2026-06-29
position_end: The exchange linking patient information systems now includes the patient register and facility list, with an independent continental assessment of it and of provincial and private solutions set for December 2025 and the in-house primary-care record in beta testing (2026-06)
note: the ministry's own replies; the assessment's findings are not held

subject: dpi.exchange
name: National Single Window for trade
milestone: No completion date given by the revenue service, September 2026
position_start: Inspection workflow with the Border Management Authority live (2023-09)
position_end: Introduced in phases with no completion date and no list of integrated agencies given by the revenue service in September 2026; the inspection workflow live since September 2023 is in phased testing with selected plant-product importers, and electronic permits and certificates, small-business declarations and inspection bookings are later phases

subject: dpi.exchange
name: One-stop border posts and digitised border systems
milestone: Works under way at Ressano Garcia, reported 2026-10-23
position_end: Named a chairship priority for the regional bloc, tied to the corridor trip monitoring system, online permitting, the electronic travel authorisation and a proposed regional tourism visa; a bilateral review with Lesotho on 9 September 2026 agreed to accelerate smart one-stop border posts at Maseru and Ficksburg. Works had begun at Ressano Garcia, on the Mozambican side of the main crossing with South Africa, on a one-stop border post integrating immigration and customs controls and their information systems, at about 980 million meticais, targeting mineral-truck transit of about five minutes against 45 to 60
note: the priority and the measure of progress are the chair's own; no baseline crossing time, target or timetable is published

subject: dpi.exchange
name: SACU customs-to-customs connectivity
milestone: Declaration matching by consignment reference, reported for 2025-26
position_end: Import and export declarations matched with customs union partners by unique consignment reference, with system messages and penalties for mismatches; partner system outages, late export data and outdated registration data reduce matching rates

subject: dpi.exchange
name: SAHPRA VigiFlow serious-adverse-event e-reporting pilot
position_end: Pilot open by invitation; no duration or mandatory date published
note: SAHPRA invited sponsors, applicants, clinical research organisations, investigators and holders of certificates of registration running clinical trials to report serious adverse events through the Uppsala Monitoring Centre's VigiFlow module, routing South African clinical-trial safety data through WHO-UMC-hosted infrastructure and adopting its reporting standard rather than a domestic one; no pilot duration, participant target, data-residency statement or transition date to mandatory e-reporting is published

subject: dpi.exchange
name: School administration system modernisation
position_start: The legacy system in use with no modernisation on file
position_end: User acceptance testing under way ahead of phased national implementation, with provincial education information officials and the state IT agency participating
note: the education data-coding standard of 2011 is the standing interoperability instrument behind it and has not been revised on the record

subject: dpi.id
name: Adults with no identity document
movement: No change, a first count with no earlier figure behind it
position_end: 4,432,923 South Africans aged 16 or over on the population register had been issued neither a green ID book nor a smart ID card (2025-11)
note: the department's own count; no breakdown by age or province is given

subject: dpi.id
name: Birth registration within 30 days
position_end: 680,555 babies registered within 30 days of birth in 2025/26 against a target of 677,000, with automation of the birth process in health facilities still planned for 2026/27
note: the department's own figure; no denominator of total births is given, so the share registered in time is not derivable

subject: dpi.id
name: Digital driving licence
milestone: Interdepartmental working group reported to Parliament, 2026-10-06
position_end: Nearest dated milestone 2027-03; the transport department told a parliamentary committee on 6 October 2026 that a Presidency-led working group with the traffic corporation and home affairs is exploring digital licences within the digital identity framework
sources: 2026-10-06-parliament-media-statement-select-committee-briefed-on-proposed-amendments-to-reg|2026-01-07 Digital driving licence coming to South Africa

subject: dpi.id
name: Draft Identification Regulations amendments
milestone: Consultation closed 2026-06-06 on a 33-day comment period
position_end: Gazetted 2026-05-04 and the comment period closed on 2026-06-06. A research organisation's submission on the closing day asked the department to suspend the regulations pending a published Digital Identity Policy, an enacted National Identification and Registration Bill and demonstrated compliance with the data-protection Act, on the ground that they create a biometric enrolment, trusted-entity accreditation and real-time verification system with no formal role for the Information Regulator
sources: 2026-05-06-digital-id-draft-regulation-gazetted|2026-06-06-research-ict-africa-submission-sa-digital-id-regulations-amendment|2026-05-09-smart-ids-go-digital-draft-rules|2026-05-29 Opinion South Africa's Digital Identity Regulations A Governance Crossroads
note: voluntary digital-ID credentials with legal parity to physical ID, trusted entities granted API access to the population register under data-sharing agreements, three assurance levels, seven-year audit logs and private-sector enrolment points; finalisation dated September 2026; criticised as likely ultra vires ahead of the NIR Bill, with no right to erasure of biometric data and no citizen visibility into access logs. The submission itself is held as a supplied PDF with no published URL, so it cannot be linked to a reader

subject: dpi.id
name: Draft regulations extending driving licence card validity to ten years
milestone: Briefed to a parliamentary committee 2026-10-06; draft gazetted for comment
position_end: Draft amendments to the National Road Traffic Regulations would extend light-vehicle licence cards from five to ten years, the department citing card-production delays and breakdowns of the card printing machine; heavy-vehicle cards and professional permits are unchanged

subject: dpi.id
name: Electronic travel authorisation
milestone: Automated risk-based adjudication described by the department, 2026-10-02
position_end: Launched by the president at OR Tambo and live at four airports — OR Tambo, Cape Town, King Shaka and Lanseria — from 2026-08-12, with 6,126 fraudulent applications rejected, put at 2.8% of pilot submissions, and full visa-type rollout targeted by end-2026; the department said in October 2026 that the system makes automated, risk-based adjudication decisions using machine learning, with a human brought in only where it detects an anomaly
sources: 2026-10-02-itweb-sa-eta-machine-learning-visa-adjudication|2026-08-16-politicsweb-ramaphosa-electronic-travel-authorisation-launch|2026-08-13-south-africa-eta-digital-travel-four-airports|2026-08-06-wheels-up-for-electronic-travel-authorisation-visas|2026-07-28-timeslive-home-affairs-eta-digital-visa-expansion|2026-07-21-schreiber-xpatweb-global-mobility-conference-keynote|2026-06-26-sa-parliamentary-question-nw3688-source-file-eta-ttos-figures|2026-05-15-schreiber-home-affairs-budget-vote-2026-27-speech|2026-02-24 South Africa makes the ETA the cornerstone of its visa reform
note: the department publishes no statistical series and the bases do not reconcile — 88,033 applications received between 2025-10-29 and 2026-01-31 in a written reply to Parliament, over 75,000 processed with nearly 4,500 rejections at the budget vote of 2026-05-15, 203,000 processed with more than 5,700 rejected at 2026-07-21, and 6,126 rejections put at 2.8% of pilot submissions on 2026-08-13. About 85% of applications are assessed automatically against a 24-hour target and checked against 40 document-authenticity parameters, and no appeal route, accuracy rate, disparate-impact testing or human-review threshold is stated

subject: dpi.id
name: Identity documents blocked on suspicion of fraud
position_end: About 300,000 identity documents blocked, the blocks sitting behind court orders where duplicate documents or people illegally in the country were detected; the minister states that the great majority of identity-theft cases involve the manual green identity book, still held by about 16 million people
note: the minister's own figure, given in a newspaper interview; the department's answer is stated as expanding the smart identity card and the electronic travel authorisation

subject: dpi.id
name: Identity theft and fraudulent identity document investigations
milestone: Figure given in a parliamentary reply, reported 2026-09-23
position_end: 21 cases of identity theft and fraudulently acquired identity documents under investigation by the department's counter-corruption and security services branch
note: the minister attributes most identity theft cases to the green identity book; no count of referrals or disciplinary outcomes is given

subject: dpi.id
name: Investigation into visa adjudication without verification
milestone: 205 visas flagged for revocation, seven disciplinary referrals
position_end: The special investigating unit found that home affairs adjudicators took payments to approve visas on fraudulent supporting documents without conducting any verification, and has flagged 205 visas for revocation and deportation with seven disciplinary referrals alongside administrative referrals to the department and criminal referrals to the prosecuting authority, under a 2024 proclamation covering almost two decades of visa and permit administration. It recommends reducing human intervention through technology and integrating home affairs systems with other departments so verifications run automatically
note: the recommendation echoes the portfolio committee's March 2026 finding that a lack of integration between departmental system interfaces was hampering investigations; the minister separately reports more than 2,000 fraudulently issued study visas and 20 officials dismissed since April 2025

subject: dpi.id
name: National digital identity (credential and wallet)
milestone: First-quarter target to start procuring hosting infrastructure missed, reported 2026-10-06
position_end: The core biometric technology live for the citizenship portal while the digital identity front end is still being built, with rollout intended during 2026 and a working single-citizen application prototype built; the minister showed the first working digital identity credential, bound to his own phone, on 1 October 2026; no public release date was given; the department's quarterly report to Parliament's home affairs committee, reported 6 October 2026, records a missed first-quarter target to sign the work order starting procurement of hosting infrastructure, after a single supplier's proposal in May and a switch to a strategic supplier model, with procurement now aimed at the second quarter
sources: 2026-10-06-problem-with-plan-for-digital-ids-in-south-africa|2026-10-01-zaf-citizen-green-id-book-end-digital-id-prototype|2026-10-02-zaf-polity-schreiber-home-affairs-quantum-leap-address|2026-02-17-schreiber-2026-state-of-the-nation-debate|2026-01-01-operation-vulindlela-phase-ii-progress-report-q3-2025-26|2026-05-20-home-affairs-828m-digital-id-budget|2026-03-26-dha-annual-performance-plan-2026-27|2026-04-21 South Africa's digital ID gets a targeted launch date|2026-03-30-dha-annual-performance-plan-2026-27-digital-identity|2025-03-11-digital-id-before-2029-elections|2026-01-30-digital-id-behind-schedule-mymzansi
note: core identity and PKI infrastructure hosted within the SARS environment, with SARB integrating on payments and eKYC; FY2026/27's only target is the hosting infrastructure itself, due 31 March 2027, with verifiable credentials via digital wallet in 2027/28 and digital identity and e-passports by 2029; facial recognition primary, fingerprints secondary

subject: dpi.id
name: Passport requirement for foreign nationals' SIM registration
position_end: Proposed that foreign nationals present passports to register SIM cards, with traceability kept when numbers change, while the government engages operators on tighter registration and tracing
note: operators began stricter SIM registration measures in July 2026, on the same account

subject: dpi.id
name: Population-register verification error rate
position_start: Failure rates of up to 50% on biometric verification hits, with responses taking up to 24 hours
position_end: An error rate well below 1% on testing of the upgraded system, rolled out to public and private users in March 2025
note: the department's own figures

subject: dpi.id
name: Revised White Paper on Citizenship, Immigration and Refugee Protection
position_end: Approved by Cabinet, anchoring civil-registration reform in turning the National Population Register into an Intelligent Population Register through biometrics, interoperability and real-time integration as the foundation for digital identity, alongside digitally enabled mandatory birth and death registration
note: a white paper rather than a bill; the identification statute it anticipates is carried separately on this ledger

subject: dpi.id
name: Road traffic regulations amendment on acceptable identification
milestone: Draft to be published for 30 days' comment, reported 2026-10-11
position_end: The transport department plans to amend the National Road Traffic Regulations so that traffic register number certificates, learner's and driving licences are no longer acceptable identification, after a 2023 check matched only 29,653 of 1,072,258 traffic register numbers, 2.7%, to the immigration identification system; the draft would also tie a traffic register number's validity to the passport and permit it was issued on, and the minister says 300,000 dormant numbers have already been blocked, with about 8,000 holders coming forward for verification by Home Affairs

subject: dpi.id
name: SARS unique digital identity system
milestone: In the SARS strategic plan for 2025-2030
position_end: The revenue service's plan for 2025 to 2030 commits it to establish a unique digital identity system linking persons and financial transactions

subject: dpi.id
name: State public key infrastructure for digital identity
milestone: Nothing deployed while Zambia and Namibia stood up national roots, reported 2026-09-11
position_end: Provided for in policy and draft regulations and promised by the presidency, with no state root of trust deployed commercially, while two neighbouring states launched national root certification authorities inside a fortnight
note: a technology publication's account; no timetable or designated root authority is published

subject: dpi.id
name: Treasury employee verification platform
position_end: A real-time biometric employee-verification portal built for the National Treasury and linked to the population register, to detect payroll records with no matching person, with go-live stated as 15 June 2026
note: no confirmation that go-live occurred, and no count of records checked or discrepancies found, is on file

subject: dpi.pay
name: Absa Digital Asset Custody
position_start: Did not exist; custody partnership with Ripple signed October 2025
position_end: Institutional custody, administration and transfer of digital assets for asset managers, non-bank financial institutions, corporates and treasuries, on Ripple's custody technology; not a retail offering
note: the bank's own account; no client count or assets held are published

subject: dpi.pay
name: Activity-based payments Authorisation Framework
status: In development, draft directive consulted November 2025
position_end: The central bank's framework to open the payment system to non-banks, issued in draft for consultation in November 2025 as a 130-page directive on specific payment activities, with final publication set for the end of November 2026
note: forward timelines as stated in a central-bank speech

subject: dpi.pay
name: Bank Zero alliance-banking platform
position_end: Live since January 2026, letting fintechs, retailers and platforms issue card products on the app-only bank's own platform; 500,000 customers of a remittance firm are being onboarded to take it past 700,000 end account holders, and the bank recorded its first break-even month in August 2026 on 275,000 direct customers
note: the bank's own figures; break-even is for one month, and new foreign-exchange capabilities await central bank approval

subject: dpi.pay
name: Capitec-Walletdoc merger conditions
position_end: Behavioural conditions agreed; Tribunal had not ruled at 2026-08-06
note: the Competition Commission recommended that the Tribunal approve Capitec Bank's R400 million acquisition of payment provider and system operator Walletdoc subject to behavioural conditions: the merged entity must make Capitec Pay available to third-party payment service providers technically and commercially capable of integrating with it, may not use confidential commercial information obtained through that access to compete against them, and must treat competing rails including PayShap Request and the Rapid Payments Programme no less favourably than Capitec Pay unless objectively justified by scheme rules or risk management

subject: dpi.pay
name: Cashless municipal service offices, Cape Town
milestone: Pilot extends to three driving licence testing centres from 2026-10-01
position_end: Six service offices cashless from 1 September 2026, and three of the city's 18 driving licence testing centres - Brackenfell, Fish Hoek and Strand - to pilot cashless transactions from 1 October 2026
note: the city is extending an existing pilot at Table Bay Mall, Durbanville and Bellville motor-vehicle registration offices to customer interaction and licensing offices at Strand, Brackenfell and Kraaifontein; no figure is published for how many residents at those counters paid in cash before the change, and nothing is stated about an alternative route for the unbanked, which is the whole of the inclusion question a cashless counter raises

subject: dpi.pay
name: CIPS participation (Standard Bank)
milestone: Went live and inaugurated at the SARB 2025-11-20
position_start: No African bank held CIPS direct-participant status
position_end: Standard Bank live as the first African bank offering CIPS transactions; RMB the settlement currency
note: three separate milestones: accredited for direct-participant qualification in April 2025 (CIPS Announcement No. 108, 2025-05-12), licensed at the Lujiazui Forum in June 2025, live and inaugurated at the South African Reserve Bank on 2025-11-20 with SARB Governor Lesetja Kganyago, PBoC Governor Pan Gongsheng and CIPS chairman Wang Hongbo present; CIPS was connected to 189 countries and territories and had processed US$12.7 trillion in H1 2025 (as at September 2025)

subject: dpi.pay
name: Commercial bank technology spending
position_end: One of the large banks put total information-technology spend for the first half of 2026 at R8,779m, up 7 per cent and 28 per cent of group expenses, within non-staff costs that grew 3 per cent to R13,143m; information-technology costs at the South African bank alone rose 6 per cent to R3,800m on investment in cybersecurity, cloud and data, partly offset by infrastructure optimisation. It also took a R200m impairment on internally generated intangible assets against nil in the prior period. Digital adoption is reported by segment rather than group-wide: in personal and private banking, digitally active customers rose 10 per cent to 3.8m against total customers of 9.9m, inside a footprint of over 13.4 million customers across 17 countries
note: one bank's own results, group-wide rather than South African, so it bounds the cost of digital migration at a single institution and not the sector. The booklet does not carry the group-wide 14 per cent rise in digitally active customers reported second-hand, nor a R2.4bn 2025 software write-down; both remain the trade press's alone

subject: dpi.pay
name: Common Monetary Area low-value cross-border EFT directive (Directive 1 of 2025)
milestone: Listed among the Reserve Bank's payment system directives
position_end: The Reserve Bank's directive governing the execution of low-value cross-border electronic funds transfers within the Common Monetary Area

subject: dpi.pay
name: Cross-border retail e-commerce exchange control framework
position_end: A draft exchange control circular letting payment aggregators partner authorised dealers for cross-border retail e-commerce payments, issued for consultation in December 2025; comments were under review in June 2026, and the circular is to be published together with the offshore-merchant payments directive

subject: dpi.pay
name: Digital-only bank results
milestone: First full-year operating profit, R370 million
position_end: The country's digital-only bank reported a R370 million normalised profit from operations for the year to 30 June 2026, reversing a R68 million loss the previous period, with client numbers up 26 per cent to 1.57 million, revenue up 31 per cent to R3.1 billion, retail deposits up 17 per cent to R27.2 billion and gross retail advances up 40 per cent to R12.9 billion. It targets R3 billion annual profit by 2029 and launches on 1 October 2026 a second phase connecting the group's banking, health, insurance and investment businesses through artificial-intelligence personalisation in a single application
note: the bank's own reported figures; no independent measure of digital-only banking share is held

subject: dpi.pay
name: Draft directive on payments to offshore merchants
position_end: A Reserve Bank draft directive on issuing and acquiring payments for goods and services from offshore merchants, put out for comment until 17 July 2026

subject: dpi.pay
name: Formal remittances from South Africa to the rest of SADC
milestone: Market assessment of 2024, supported by the Reserve Bank
position_end: Formal outflows of over R19 billion in 15.7 million transactions in 2024, up from under R6 billion in 2016, with Zimbabwe, Lesotho, Malawi and Mozambique taking nearly 90%; a USD200 transfer cost 8.3% on the weighted regional average excluding Malawi and the Common Monetary Area, against 7.6% in 2021

subject: dpi.pay
name: Fraud complaints at the banking ombud
position_start: 15,412 banking cases opened in 2024, fraud about 30% of complaints
position_end: Fraud complaints almost doubled from 2024 to 2025, with 3,651 fraud-related cases closed in 2025
note: the ombud says the rise is industry-wide, not tied to one bank

subject: dpi.pay
name: Move of SADC regional payments under R100,000 to TCIB
position_end: Qualifying regional payments under R100,000 to move from SADC-RTGS to the TCIB transactional clearing scheme by the end of April 2027
note: forward timeline as stated in a central-bank speech

subject: dpi.pay
name: MTN MoMo outbound remittance corridors
position_end: 25 wallet corridors from South Africa to ten African countries, reaching some 200 million wallets held by 39 partners in 24 countries; payments flow outbound only

subject: dpi.pay
name: National Financial Ombud Scheme (NFO)
position_end: A unified ombud for banking, credit, life and non-life complaints, which published its first annual report for 2024; its banking division returned more than R60m to consumers in 2025, most of it in fraud refunds

subject: dpi.pay
name: National Payment System Regulatory and Oversight Report
position_end: The central bank's annual account of payment-system regulation and oversight, issued for 2023/24, 2024/25 and 2025/26; the 2025/26 edition records 14 banks on PayShap and the move away from the payments association as the payment system management body

subject: dpi.pay
name: Onsite card checkout for Shopify merchants
position_end: Shoppers pay by card inside the Shopify merchant checkout without redirection, alongside a Shopify integration for the provider's in-store terminal
note: the provider's own announcement; no merchant count or payment volume is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: Open finance policy position
milestone: Stated under development in the conduct regulator's 2026 regulation plan
position_end: Being developed by the conduct regulator with the Intergovernmental Fintech Working Group under the Treasury's guidance, after a series of working papers on use cases, API standardisation, competition and costs; legislative interventions are expected but their nature and timing are not set

subject: dpi.pay
name: Payments Ecosystem Modernisation credential and wallet
milestone: Activity-based licensing model set out publicly, 2026-09-09
position_end: Both the rules of participation and the infrastructure are being rebuilt together, three payments executives said at a Johannesburg roundtable on 9 September 2026: a proposed activity-based regulatory model would let non-banks and fintechs offer payment services directly rather than through a sponsoring bank, alongside richer payment data and faster cross-border rails.
note: an industry roundtable account rather than a regulator's publication; no draft licensing instrument, commencement date or capital requirement for the proposed activity categories is held

subject: dpi.pay
name: Payments group return to profit
position_start: A group net loss of R1.63 billion, about US$91 million, in the year to June 2025
position_end: A group net profit of R47.3 million, about US$2.8 million at the R16.91 average rate the company used for its 2026 year, for the year to June 2026 - stated by its executive chairman as full-year net profitability for the first time since the group was created in 2022 out of a predecessor company, and accompanied by a brand refresh under a single identity.
note: company-reported results carried by a trade publication; no revenue, transaction volume or segment split is held, and the swing from a R1.63bn loss is not decomposed into trading and non-trading items

subject: dpi.pay
name: PEMKey payment credential ecosystem
milestone: Sandbox open subject to approval, presented to industry September 2026
position_end: A central-bank programme under payments ecosystem modernisation to establish secure, reusable digital credentials across payments, building on foundational credentials; its sandbox participants are not published and whether the state digital ID will be accepted is not stated

subject: dpi.pay
name: Postbank authorisation as a bank
milestone: Directed to file a new section 12 application; not submitted as at 2026-10-15
position_end: Directed by the Prudential Authority to submit a new application to establish a bank under section 12 of the Banks Act, replacing its 2016 authorisation; not yet submitted and no date given, with recapitalisation (a request before National Treasury), banking-system modernisation and a bank controlling company outstanding

subject: dpi.pay
name: Remittance cost, South Africa to Zimbabwe
milestone: IMF and World Bank corridor diagnostic
position_end: Sending money from South Africa to Zimbabwe cost 12.7% on average in the first quarter of 2024 against the G20 target of 3%, with cash dependence, AML/CFT rules and access requirements blamed

subject: dpi.pay
name: Renminbi Clearing Bank of Africa
position_start: Did not exist; CIPS participation only (live 2025-11-20)
position_end: Standard Bank and ICBC jointly authorised as RMB clearing bank for Africa, with operational capacity in the 19 African countries where Standard Bank Group operates
note: the first RMB clearing bank named after a continent and the first jointly operated by two commercial banks; ICBC already acts as RMB clearing bank in 12 countries and holds a strategic equity stake in Standard Bank Group; the 19 countries are not enumerated in either the PBoC-sourced account or the bank's own as at 2026-08-04, and the designation was made by one foreign central bank with no African regulator party to it

subject: dpi.pay
name: Retail acquisition of an informal-trade payments network
position_end: an initial 51% interest acquired with effect from 14 August 2026 in a point-of-sale and vending network installed behind the counter in spaza shops and informal stores, selling prepaid airtime, electricity, gaming and entertainment
note: financial terms are undisclosed and the acquirer has not completed the initial accounting for the combination

subject: dpi.pay
name: Retail central bank digital currency
note: the SARB's published position is that a retail CBDC has no compelling case yet and that the everyday rails come first; wholesale DLT work ran through Project Khokha 1 (2018) and Khokha 2 (2022)

subject: dpi.pay
name: SARB Interchange Determination Project
milestone: Industry papers being taken into account, reported 2026-09-28
position_end: A central bank project to determine card interchange fees; a non-bank payment providers' association says the SARB has confirmed its two cost-of-payments and interchange papers are being taken into account
note: the account is the association's own; no draft determination or timetable is held

subject: dpi.pay
name: SARS tax and customs payment channels
position_end: Tax and customs are paid electronically, through eFiling, EFT quoting a payment reference number, the SARS MobiApp or card; cash deposits at banks for customs and excise were withdrawn on 24 July 2023 and customs electronic declarants must pay through eFiling

subject: dpi.pay
name: Scan to Pay QR scheme
milestone: Added to a handset maker's wallet, reported 31 August 2026
position_end: More than 600,000 acceptance locations and more than 19 million inclusions in consumer banking, fintech and financial service provider applications, and now available in a handset maker's wallet on eligible devices, that wallet having launched locally in November 2022
note: the acceptance and inclusion figures are the scheme provider's, carried in a handset maker's statement, with no transaction volume or value published and no relation stated to the national payment code standard

subject: dpi.pay
name: TCIB instant payments corridor, South Africa to Zambia
position_end: The first instant low-value cross-border payment corridor from South Africa to Zambia on the regional TCIB scheme, opened by the licensed regional clearing operator with two remittance firms joining as participants

subject: dpi.pay
name: Transfer of PASA's payment-system functions to the SARB and PayInc
position_start: Functions held by the Payments Association of South Africa
position_end: The last of the payments association's functions transferred to the central bank and the payments utility on 2 September 2026
note: reported by a non-bank payment providers' association, which gives the date without a year; no transfer instrument is held

subject: dpi.pay
name: Vending and metering estate moving into electricity trading
position_end: A vending, payments and municipal-metering operator is pushing its estate up the electricity value chain on a multi-year electricity trading licence granted by the energy regulator in February 2026
note: a payments and metering estate becoming an energy trader is a use of the same rails for a different market; no traded volume, customer count or municipal agreement is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: Visa domestic processing data centre, Johannesburg
position_end: The card scheme's first data centre in Africa, at an undisclosed Johannesburg site, processing all domestic transactions in the country, as part of a stated R1 billion investment
note: the company's own account; build cost and site are not disclosed

subject: dpi.pay
name: Wise foreign exchange authorisation
milestone: Category 2 authorisation from the Reserve Bank, reported 2026-10-16
position_end: A UK money-transfer firm, already partnered with a domestic bank, authorised by the Reserve Bank as a category 2 dealer to send money abroad
note: the approval date is not given

subject: dpi.pay
name: ZARP rand stablecoin
position_end: A rand-pegged stablecoin issued since 2019, with about R74.6m of tokens in circulation against R92.8m of reserves on 21 September 2026
note: circulation and reserve figures as reported, not audited

subject: dpi.pay
name: ZARU rand-backed stablecoin
milestone: Live on Circle's Arc blockchain as a founding StableFX pair, 2026-09-22
position_end: Listed on Luno Global 2026-08-07 and integrated into a merchant payments provider's infrastructure on 19 August; on 22 September it went live on Circle's Arc blockchain as a founding pair on Circle's StableFX platform, trading against USDC with atomic settlement, with Luno the primary venue and Standard Bank and Absa named among the network's banking partners
note: issued by authorised financial services provider BlockTower and listed on Luno Global on 2026-08-07 for customers in South Africa, Nigeria, Kenya and Uganda, with Sanlam Specialised Asset Management holding the reserves and Moore Johannesburg attesting them monthly; the quoted pairs are ZARU/USDT and ZARU/USDC, so the on-chain liquidity of the rand token is denominated in dollar tokens; the account of growing merchant use is the issuer's own, with no transaction count or value published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Beneficial ownership declaration
position_start: Declaration required with no simplified channel on file
position_end: A simplified online beneficial-ownership declaration in service, with more than 23,000 declarations processed by the notice date; an upgraded disclosure module launched on 29 September 2026 gives law enforcement agencies - the police, the investigating directorate, the special investigating unit and the prosecuting authority among them - real-time access to company ownership information, with search and connection-mapping
note: the companies commission's own figure at three weeks; no compliance rate against the register as a whole is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Births and Deaths Registration Act 51 of 1992
position_end: In force as the statutory basis for the registration of births and deaths, the legal foundation of the civil register that feeds the population register
note: held as an excerpt; the white paper approved in April 2026 proposes digitally enabled mandatory registration under it

subject: dpi.registry
name: Blocked identity numbers
position_end: 2,202,368 identity numbers unblocked in a national review of identities blocked before November 2022

subject: dpi.registry
name: Central Supplier Database
movement: No change, a first supplier count with no earlier figure behind it
position_end: The National Treasury's single register of suppliers to the state, checking tax clearance with SARS, identity with Home Affairs, bank accounts and company registration; 939,237 registered suppliers at 31 March 2025

subject: dpi.registry
name: Child Protection Register
position_end: The social development department's register of people unsuitable to work with children listed 12,596 individuals in July 2024, and access was widened so employers can screen applicants

subject: dpi.registry
name: Companies register
milestone: More than two million active entities on the register, 2025-26
position_end: The companies commission's register of companies and other entities, holding more than two million active entities, with about 40% of its processes automated on its own account

subject: dpi.registry
name: Deeds registered on the electronic deeds system
position_end: No deed had been registered end to end on the electronic deeds registration system by November 2025; 16.9 million documents had been digitised and deeds registered since 2014 are held electronically

subject: dpi.registry
name: Electronic deeds registration system
position_start: The 2019 Act in force with the amended framework not commenced
position_end: Sections of the 2024 amendment in operation from 1 September 2025 and the schedule of deeds office fees replaced with a R52 lodgement fee and revised transfer-fee bands, effective one month after publication
note: the statute creating the electronic register dates from 2019; how much registration runs on it is carried on the electronic deeds measure row

subject: dpi.registry
name: General Laws anti-money-laundering amendment bill
position_end: Published, requiring reporting of material beneficial-ownership discrepancies, deregistration after prolonged failure to file required registers, and tribunal review of administrative fines; not enacted
note: the enforcement half of the beneficial-ownership registers reported beside it, and it is a bill rather than a statute

subject: dpi.registry
name: Health Patient Registration System
position_start: In 3,220 public facilities by August 2023, holding over 68 million registrations of which about 32.5 million were verified against Home Affairs (2024)
position_end: Rolled out in 3,280 facilities, with biometric registration in 249 of them verified in real time against the National Population Register in collaboration with Home Affairs (August 2025)
note: registrations exceed the population, so the count is of records, not people

subject: dpi.registry
name: Home Affairs civic records digitisation
position_end: Over 49 million paper civic records digitised since 2023, with a further 25 million targeted, so that amendments can be made without the eight-week manual process (2025-07)
note: the department's own figures

subject: dpi.registry
name: Intelligent Population Register
milestone: Anchored in the approved white paper
position_end: The conversion of the population register into an intelligent population register anchored in the Cabinet-approved white paper, on biometrics, interoperability and real-time integration, with the core biometric technology live for the citizenship portal
note: cast as migration control - biometrics for every person, the green ID book to be de-recognised and the Traffic Registration Number abolished, under a Cabinet comprehensive approach for migration management; DHA has tendered a biometric case-management system and 600 handheld readers

subject: dpi.registry
name: KwaZulu-Natal Public Works property finding portal
position_end: A provincial portal listing state-owned property after an audit of all 10,067 assets and the release of a first batch of 81 unused buildings and land parcels, for organisations and developers to identify assets for lease or re-use and for residents to log complaints about them; announced for live launch on 7 October 2026

subject: dpi.registry
name: Master Health Facility List
position_end: The register of public and private health establishments, 51,131 listed with a working group reviewing a standard establishment-registry framework (2023-09)

subject: dpi.registry
name: National Integrated Social Information System
milestone: Reported undeveloped at a June 2025 dialogue
position_end: The system meant to harmonise social protection data remains undeveloped, while the relief grant checks eligibility against nine state databases and no legal framework for data sharing exists (2025-06)

subject: dpi.registry
name: National Population Register
note: cast as migration control - biometrics for every person, the green ID book to be de-recognised and the Traffic Registration Number abolished, under a Cabinet comprehensive approach for migration management; DHA has tendered a biometric case-management system and 600 handheld readers

subject: dpi.registry
name: NPO Registration and Compliance Monitoring Online System
milestone: Legacy NPO system switched off 15 October 2026, announced 2026-10-13
position_start: Introduced on 1 September 2025 in three phases, the legacy registration and reporting system kept running beside it after technical problems
position_end: The single channel for registered non-profit organisations from 15 October 2026, when the social development department switches off its legacy system and stops accepting manually submitted documents at its offices; organisations file registrations, annual compliance reports and statutory documents online or through a mobile app, and the department says the system integrates with the companies registry, the revenue service and home affairs
note: the integrations are the department's own description; no count of organisations migrated or of records not yet visible on the new system is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Online birth registration at health facilities
position_end: Home Affairs registers births online at health facilities, 161 of them covering about 68% of births in November 2023, and is working to equip 1,445 facilities to register births immediately (December 2025)

subject: dpi.registry
name: Partnership beneficial owner register
milestone: Structured register and filing workflow operationalised
position_end: A structured partnership beneficial-owner register and electronic filing workflow in service, generating persistent partnership and partner reference numbers for later validation and pre-population
note: the revenue service's register runs beside the companies commission's, and no source states whether the two reconcile

subject: dpi.registry
name: Personal income tax register
position_end: 27.1 million individuals on the personal income tax register in March 2024, with 488,118 active VAT vendors and 1.17 million companies assessed for 2022

subject: dpi.registry
name: SARS Client Information System
milestone: Single tax and customs profile, in place since 2014
position_end: One consolidated profile per taxpayer for income tax, employee taxes, VAT and customs and excise, implemented in 2014; companies registered with CIPC are registered for income tax automatically through a direct interface

subject: dpi.registry
name: SOCPEN social grant payment system
position_end: Confirmed in a ministerial reply as the system administering grant payments to more than 18 million monthly beneficiaries
note: the largest beneficiary count of any system on this ledger, and the repository holds no architecture, uptime or modernisation record for it

subject: dpi.registry
name: Statutory duty to build a national address database
position_end: The post office amendment act of 2024 inserts a duty on the post office to implement a national address system and to develop and maintain a national address database. It is the clearest legal basis yet for a national address register. Commencement is by presidential proclamation, and the government's own status record for the act still marks it to be proclaimed, so the mandate is enacted and not yet operative.

subject: dpi.registry
name: Tax Administration Act and its 2026 amendment
position_start: The 2011 Act in force as the register's statutory basis
position_end: The amendment enacted, creating the enabling framework for a simplified customs regime for door-to-door express imports and exports and for a voluntary value-added-tax electronic reporting system
note: the electronic reporting system the amendment enables is voluntary, and no commencement or uptake figure is on file

subject: dpi.registry
name: Tax reference number enquiry service
position_end: A self-service channel on the revenue service's filing platform for retrieving and verifying a taxpayer reference number, documented in an external guide
note: a service guide rather than a service report; no usage figure is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Uncollected identity documents
position_end: 360,000 uncollected at Home Affairs offices (2026-07-31)
note: Home Affairs opened every office nationwide from 08:00 to 17:00 on 1 and 2 August 2026 for the final voter registration weekend, stating that 360,000 identity documents sat uncollected; a valid identity document is a precondition of registering to vote, and the department published no figure for how long the documents have been waiting and no breakdown by office or province

subject: dpi.mis
name: Basic Accounting System
milestone: Version 6 chart of accounts cut over 2025-04-01
position_end: The national and provincial accounting system moved to version 6 of the standard chart of accounts on 1 April 2025 with capacity and interface failures; 160 of 161 departments closed 2024/25 and 133 of 162 closed April 2025, 29 forced closed
note: the system the Integrated Financial Management System was meant to replace

subject: dpi.mis
name: Court Online
milestone: Older KwaZulu-Natal High Court matters to move onto CaseLines from 20 July 2026
position_end: The judiciary's e-filing and CaseLines evidence system ran in 19 courts by August 2025, beginning with Pretoria and Johannesburg in September 2022 and funded through the integrated justice system; it has been mandatory for KwaZulu-Natal High Court cases since 1 April 2025

subject: dpi.mis
name: District Health Management Information System Policy
milestone: Issued by the national health department, 2011
position_end: The national health information policy sets seven priority areas for the district health information system and rules on data ownership, access control and data security

subject: dpi.mis
name: Geospatial Information Management Strategy
position_start: Did not exist on the repository
position_end: Moving toward implementation at its first provincial roadshow, with a live geospatial dashboard demonstrated and work under way with one province and one metro on spatial data governance and interoperability
note: the national spatial data instrument that the mining cadastre and the deeds register would both sit under; no adoption instrument or budget is published

subject: dpi.mis
name: Home Affairs revenue administration system
milestone: Tender revised and re-advertised, reported 31 August 2026
position_start: Advertised in June 2026 over a generic 400-plus site footprint, with standalone kiosks and the department's online channel listed as transaction channels
position_end: Re-advertised over a two-tier footprint of 275 fixed sites and 230 mobile units, with point-of-sale devices and mobile offices as the primary transaction channels and payment processing and reconciliation tied to them; the system is to handle collection, reconciliation and Basic Accounting System reporting with real-time interfaces to the service manager, live-capture, automated citizen processor and branch queuing systems, and only suppliers on the state IT agency's RFB 1183 transversal contract may bid
note: a tender, not an award: no value, closing date, bidder or delivery schedule is held, and the restriction to one transversal contract narrows the field before bidding

subject: dpi.mis
name: Integrated Financial Management System
milestone: Cloud move under discussion with the supplier, reply to Parliament 2025-06-26
position_start: In development, stalled, with R2.6bn spent since 2005 (2024-09)
position_end: Still not in service: the Treasury said in June 2025 that talks with the supplier on moving from an on-premises installation to a cloud platform had been aligned with the presidency's government digitisation programme, and that it would brief Parliament on the proposed direction when ready
note: the Treasury's own reply

subject: dpi.mis
name: Integrated human resource management ERP for the public service
position_end: The Treasury approved a deviation on 19 November 2024 letting the public service department implement an integrated HRM enterprise resource planning solution, subject to integration, compliance and funding conditions; the department says planning must mature before deployment, after the financial management system project delayed it

subject: dpi.mis
name: Land administration systems
milestone: Carried in the department's annual performance plan
position_end: Land administration and spatial systems carried as departmental commitments in the annual performance plan, against an annual report recording the state of the deeds and cadastral estate
note: both are held as excerpts and neither carries a system name, cost or delivery date

subject: dpi.mis
name: Mining Cadastre System
position_end: The provincial pilot reported complete to Parliament, a spatially defined rights register intended to improve the digital administration and transparency of mining licensing
note: no national rollout date, cost or licence-volume figure is published

subject: dpi.mis
name: National Digital Health Strategy 2019-2024
position_end: No successor strategy held
note: published by the National Department of Health with a ministerial foreword dated 2019-05-15, superseding the eHealth Strategy 2012-2016 and setting nine strategic interventions to 2024; its investment intervention proposes a national grant for digital health established with National Treasury targeting a proportionate allocation of three to five per cent of health expenditure, and it commits to a Master Patient Index for all South Africans, conformance testing of all health information systems, a health play store and a review of digital-health governance structures by 2020; the wiki holds nothing measuring what any of it delivered

subject: dpi.mis
name: National Digital Health Strategy, revised
milestone: Promised for the fourth quarter of 2025/26; not released as at July 2026
position_end: The 2019-2024 strategy under review, with the revised strategy promised for publication in the fourth quarter of the 2025/26 financial year; a 2025-2029 successor was referenced in a Global Fund case study but had not been released as at July 2026
note: no revised strategy is held

subject: dpi.mis
name: NSFAS student funding system
milestone: Funding restored for 182 TUT students after qualification-code corrections, 2026-09-13
position_end: Under administration; ICT named the largest operational risk, and the data-sharing defect between an institution's financial aid office and the scheme has now been documented in a single case: more than 300 self-reported helpdesk cases at Tshwane University of Technology over defunding under the N+ rule, of which 182 had funding restored in September 2026 once the university corrected qualification codes. A further 1,212 students placed in accredited accommodation after the scheme's portal closed, and 115 approved for funding after it closed, have not had accommodation costs paid and have been referred to the board for investigation
note: the administrator's stabilisation plan, submitted to the minister of higher education and training in the week to 2026-08-07, states that "ICT is NSFAS's biggest operational risk, as it is fragmented, manual and not fit for purpose"; the same submission reports 66 major audit findings and a disclaimer audit opinion from the Auditor-General, 115 overdue internal audit findings and nine material irregularities, five of them data or systems defects; the scheme was placed under administration in May 2026 and the governance failures referred to the Special Investigating Unit

subject: dpi.mis
name: Police case docket systems (CAS and ICDMS)
milestone: Minister's reply of December 2025 on docket checks and halted statistics
position_end: Dockets are registered on the police's crime administration system under a 2011 instruction, and the electronic docket system was reported live at 998 stations in May 2021 with 159 waiting on network upgrades; the 2025-2030 strategic plan commits to full docket integration and blames the state IT agency for delays, and a ministerial reply of December 2025 records victim-data errors halting the women-and-children crime statistics

subject: dpi.mis
name: Police incident management solution
position_end: The state IT agency is procuring a 36-month incident management solution for the police, whose tender states the service has no single integrated system for registering reported incidents

subject: dpi.mis
name: SARS automated customs processing system
position_end: One automated, centralised processing system for all commercial trade across the borders replaced some 26 legacy and paper-based systems, cutting paper by up to 95%

subject: dpi.mis
name: SARS personal income tax auto-assessment
position_start: 5.8 million taxpayers auto-assessed at the opening of the 2025 filing season (July 2025)
position_end: More than 6.9 million returns auto-assessed by 30 September 2026, up 20% on the previous year, after auto-assessment was widened to some provisional taxpayers and notices were served through WhatsApp

subject: dpi.mis
name: Social work integrated management system external referral portal (Western Cape)
milestone: External referral portal opened to mandated reporters
position_end: The Western Cape's social work integrated management system now accepts secure external reports of child abuse and neglect, identified or anonymous, from the categories of professional the Children's Act obliges to report - health professionals, legal practitioners, teachers, traditional leaders and religious leaders - routing them into the provincial case-management system rather than through a separate channel
note: a provincial system, not a national one; no referral volume, response time or integration with the national child protection register is stated

subject: dpi.mis
name: Transversal financial systems (BAS, PERSAL, LOGIS and Vulindlela)
position_end: The accounting system of 1992, the payroll system of 1994, the logistics system of 1998 and the Vulindlela management information layer of 1997 remain the core transversal systems of national and provincial departments, with in-house Treasury tools drawing on them to automate reporting to Parliament

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Asylum intention-registration and appointment system
milestone: To be operational by 10 November 2026, announced 2026-10-11
position_end: An online, biometric intention-registration and appointment system for asylum applicants, issuing a receipt that records personal particulars, biometrics, a reference number and an appointment, with assisted registration at Refugee Reception Offices; biometrics are to be checked against earlier rejected applications and travel documents verified; announced by the Inter-Ministerial Committee on Migration to be operational by 10 November 2026
note: announced alongside government's decision to seek a court supervisory order on implementing the Constitutional Court judgment of 7 July 2026; the minister put the asylum appeals backlog at about 120,000, a figure he said was to be confirmed

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Batho Pele AI chatbot
position_end: DPSA-Meta-Juicetel partnership built on Meta's Llama models, providing policy, circular and legislation lookups to citizens and public servants; nine official languages targeted; explicitly decision-support only, with no decision-making authority

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Border Management Authority Port Health Management System
position_start: Port health requests submitted by shipping agents by e-mail
position_end: An end-to-end platform for port health service requests, document upload, inspections, free pratique applications, digital endorsements, invoicing and payment, behind single sign-on and role-based access, piloted at Durban Harbour (2026-09)
note: no timetable is given for rollout to other ports of entry

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Border Management Authority Vehicle Targeting System
milestone: Launched at Lebombo 2026-10-18; live since 1 April 2026
position_end: Number-plate cameras check vehicles against stolen, cloned, fraud and unconsented-finance records and alert border guards on handheld devices; deployed at Maseru Bridge, Lebombo and Vioolsdrif in April 2026, Beitbridge and Ficksburg in August and Caledonspoort in September, with 83 vehicles worth R46.6 million recovered in six months and eight land ports planned by the end of February 2027
note: Equipment is on loan from the International Vehicle Identification Desk

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Courts digitisation project
milestone: Referred to the special investigating unit and the police priority crimes unit, 2026-08-13
