position_end: Records storage has been outsourced to a private contractor since 2021 across three provinces; on 13 August 2026 the justice minister referred the project to the special investigating unit and the police priority crimes unit after the contractor denied the department access to its own records at the Master of the High Court in Pretoria
note: no contract value, term, custody arrangement or data-protection provision for the outsourced court records is held, and a department locked out of its own records is a custody failure before it is a procurement one

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Digital matric certificate
note: MyMzansi's first credential use case, built with Umalusi, with pilot architecture and the verification approach in testing; the September 2026 target hardens the pilot into a production platform rather than launching it

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Digital Transformation of Government Roadmap
milestone: Phase one due to close February 2027, stated by the minister 2026-09-21
position_end: In force, organised in four initiatives; its first phase closes in February 2027, and the minister states that government digital systems remain fragmented
note: approved by Cabinet 2025-03-26 and publicly launched 2025-05-12; Cabinet's own diagnosis names interdepartmental coordination, outdated systems, overlapping mandates and limited skills - institutional fragmentation rather than technology

subject: dpi.govtech
name: District Health Information System
milestone: Three-year hosting and support bid issued 2026-07-24
position_end: An aggregated service-delivery information system used at facility, district, provincial and national level, run as nine provincial instances synchronised to a national one; the health department issued a bid on 24 July 2026 for three years' hosting, maintenance and enhancement; in Eastern Cape all 860 public facilities used it by March 2020, with 99.5% of expected monthly reports received in a sample of 265; no national count of clinics capturing their own data is published

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Electoral Commission results system
milestone: Audit by party-designated experts, 5 to 12 October 2026
position_end: End-to-end functionality testing concluded for the 4 November 2026 local government elections, with contesting parties to get direct access to test it through their own independent experts from 5 to 12 October 2026; the leaderboards at the results operation centre malfunctioned for about two hours in 2024; the commission opened the system to audit by ICT experts designated by four parties from 5 to 12 October 2026, having concluded an independent external audit of it
note: the commission's own account at a party code-of-conduct event; no test report or independent assessment is held

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Electronic death registration system
milestone: Landscape analysis for the medical research council, October 2022
position_end: No electronic system: death notification runs on paper from the certifying practitioner through Home Affairs to the statistics agency, and an electronic medical certificate of cause of death was modelled, with options, in a 2022 landscape analysis for the medical research council; no build is on record

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Electronic entry registration and biometric tracking at ports of entry
milestone: Stated by the migration ministers' committee, 2026-10-26; no timetable
position_end: Planned electronic registration of entrants at modernised ports, recording visa details and phone numbers, with SMS reminders before visas expire and fingerprints added to a broader biometric tracking system; no timetable or instrument stated

subject: dpi.govtech
name: eTender Publication Portal
status: Implemented, electronic submission in limited use
milestone: Electronic bid submission in use, Treasury account of September 2026
position_start: Tender phase only, fragmented and with low compliance (assessment of August 2024)
position_end: 31,998 opportunities advertised and 17,893 awards reported on the portal in 2024/25; by September 2026 it also carried procurement plans, contracts and electronic bid submission used by some organs of state, with an open-contracting data feed running from February 2017

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Gauteng online school admissions
position_end: 2027 intake opened 2026-08-05
note: grade 1 and grade 8 applications, introduced 2016; the department reported over 1 000 applications on the opening morning; it carries a documented record of concurrency failures under load, late communication with parents, learners unplaced at the start of the academic year and manipulation by officials, and frames a better system as a future intention

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Gauteng public-transport operating-licence digital system
position_end: The provincial transport department launched a digital system to clear its operating-licence backlog after six to eight months of testing with e-hailing, taxi and bus operators, municipalities and law enforcement, with e-hailing operators first in line to regularise; no backlog figure is stated

subject: dpi.govtech
name: GovTech maturity classification
milestone: The 2025 edition placed the country in Group B
position_start: Group B of four on the 2022 edition (2023-03)
position_end: Group B, significant maturity, on the 2025 edition of the World Bank index (2025-12)
note: groups, not ranks; the index scores 48 indicators over four pillars and the 2025 edition publishes no country score in the held text

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Home Affairs self-service kiosks
status: In development, procured but not deployed
milestone: Found undeployed on a committee oversight visit, reported 2026-10-17
position_start: Launched as a project in May 2024
position_end: Members found the kiosks procured but never deployed, with licence costs still running; the briefing was postponed when the director-general and chief financial officer did not attend, and no total spend was disclosed

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Home Affairs system downtime
milestone: 2025/26 figures given in a departmental statement and a parliamentary reply
position_end: 13,867 hours in 2025/26, a 61% reduction, with provincial gains ranging from 79% in the Free State to 41% in North West; the population register's own downtime fell from 14,720 to 11,479 hours, a 22% improvement. The department attributes it to the state IT agency moving from a bronze to a silver service level, 226 links migrated to fibre, 182 offices moved to a web service manager and 439 offices running on the identification system
note: the parliamentary reply is the fuller record and separates population-register downtime, which improved far less than the front-office figure the department led with

subject: dpi.govtech
name: IEC digital voter registration (WhatsApp and online portal)
position_end: 1.7m registration transactions over the final weekend; 291,016 first-time registrations
note: the Electoral Commission launched voter registration inside WhatsApp on 2026-08-04, three days before the registration deadline for the November local government elections, running one-time-password authentication, identity-document upload, address verification and voting-station confirmation over Meta's platform; the online portal alone carried 238,000 of the first-time registrations and 46% of all new registrations were by people under 29; no statement on data handling, and none on a fallback if the channel fails, accompanied the launch

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Inmate communication system, 243 correctional centres
position_end: A fifteen-year tender advertised for design, supply, installation, integration, operation and maintenance across 243 correctional centres, replacing copper telephony that has deteriorated beyond support
note: the Department of Correctional Services incarcerates about 166,000 people and states that the existing copper system is no longer supported; the solution is to integrate with the inmate cash system for airtime purchase, with monitoring, recording, data storage, security and compliance in scope. No contract value is published, a non-compulsory briefing was set for 2026-08-27 and bids close 2026-09-14, so nothing is awarded

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Integrated justice system programme
milestone: Auditor-General's report presented to Parliament's justice committee 2026-10-06
position_end: The Auditor-General told Parliament's justice committee, in a report presented on 6 October 2026, that the programme has not achieved its vision after about R4.9bn spent over a decade, citing unclear accountability, fragmented oversight and limited progress on a new digital transformation and modernisation strategy, with cybersecurity and access-control weaknesses across the portfolio's systems and 63 of 506 planned network upgrades completed by 31 August 2026

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Minimum Interoperability Standards and GWEA
position_end: The sixth revision of the minimum interoperability standards framework is the standing instrument, issued by the state IT agency under the public service minister, and the successor architecture is in development

subject: dpi.govtech
name: MyMzansi single citizen application
milestone: R150m allocated to the Presidency's digital services unit, 2026 adjusted estimates
position_end: Production-ready pilot, with the digital matric certificate as first use case; the 2026 adjusted estimates allocate R150m to the Presidency's digital services unit behind it
sources: 2026-10-21-sa-mymzansi-citizen-services-r150m|2026-08-03-itweb-mymzansi-production-ready-vulindlela-q1|2025-11-09 Behind the speedy MyMzansi screens and the Presidency's race to build a digital government|2026-02-13-sona-2026-digital-mega-platform
note: progressed from proof of concept to a production-ready pilot with governance arrangements in place; the digital matric certificate is the first credential use case; stable platform, matric credential integration and the shared Gov.za platform are targeted September 2026, with Justice, SAPS and Master's Office use cases March 2027

subject: dpi.govtech
name: National electronic government procurement system
milestone: Phased build under the Public Procurement Act 2024; end-to-end open tendering targeted for 2027/28
position_end: Being developed in phases under the Public Procurement Act 2024, with end-to-end open tendering targeted for 2027/28 and a digitised state procurement system by 2030; the Treasury says the current system is largely paper-based

subject: dpi.govtech
name: National Health Insurance information architecture
milestone: NHI Phase 2 running 2026-2028, with the Act's passage before the Constitutional Court (2026-08)
position_end: In force; no implementation measurement held, with the scheme it underpins in Phase 2 and its enabling Act under constitutional challenge
note: the architecture the NHI rests on is defined inside the gazetted 2021 Health Normative Standards Framework for Interoperability in Digital Health rather than in a document of its own: a Federated Health Information Architecture hybrid of local and shared infrastructure, with central patient, provider and facility registries, shared clinical repositories and a National Health Information Exchange, built on IHE profiles, HL7 and FHIR; it supersedes the 2014 HNSF, and states that semantic interoperability remains an ongoing national undertaking with value sets to be published in implementation guides in due time. As at 2026-08 the scheme is in Phase 2, running to 2028, the Board of Healthcare Funders and the Western Cape government are challenging the Act's public-participation process in the Constitutional Court with judgment reserved since May, and the department is still building the national Health Patient Registration System

subject: dpi.govtech
name: National payment code standard (QR+)
milestone: Pilot set for the first quarter of 2027, stated 2026-10-20
position_end: v1.2 tested with an eight-bank cohort; the central bank set a QR+ interoperable merchant-code pilot for the first quarter of 2027

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Online candidate nomination system
milestone: Governing party's court challenge lost, reported 2026-09-23
position_end: In use for the local government elections; the governing party lost its court challenge claiming that glitches prevented it submitting its full candidate lists, and still says its capturers saw glitches, which the commission denies. The commission's audit trail shows no system activity in two of the six disputed councils in the final two hours, with 2,274 candidates from 45 parties captured but never submitted as final
note: the admission is the party's own at a media briefing; how many lists or identity numbers were affected, whether the system validates identity numbers against the population register, and what the electoral commission did about it are not stated

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Online Verification Service
position_end: Running since 2013 and now priced: R10 per real-time verification and R1 per batch field under section 21(2), free to state departments, municipalities and statutory bodies, in force 1 July 2025, with the revenue earmarked for the system's maintenance
sources: 2025-06-23-identification-regulations-fourteenth-amendment-gazette-52893|2025-06-23-dha-npr-verification-service-pricing-correction|2025-07-06 Home Affairs on launch of world-class new identity verification service and cost

subject: dpi.govtech
name: PayInc and the SARB stake
position_end: Bank-owned utility; non-bank shareholding ruled out (2026-07-31)
note: the Governor told the Bank's 106th ordinary general meeting on 2026-07-31 that the SARB "would have preferred to have 100% of PayInc because we want PayInc to be a payment utility. So we're not looking at bringing others in there"; Absa's chief executive put the installed base at 39 participating banks and more than 480 non-bank payment service providers

subject: dpi.govtech
name: PayShap
position_end: 905m transactions by 2026-05

subject: dpi.govtech
name: SARS digital self-service channel use
position_end: USSD requests rose to 22.4 million in 2025/26 from 14.9 million, WhatsApp requests to 4.4 million from 1.8 million and online queries to 6.9 million, with digital platforms available 99.76% of the time; 88.5% of taxpayers used digital self-service in 2023/24

subject: dpi.govtech
name: SARS eSourcing procurement portal
position_end: The revenue service's own tendering portal, drawing supplier data from the Central Supplier Database, accepting only electronic bids since 1 April 2018

subject: dpi.govtech
name: SITA procurement from small and designated suppliers
movement: No change, a first count with no earlier figure behind it
position_end: R183 million spent with small, medium and micro enterprises and designated groups between 1 April and 31 July 2026, 49% of available procurement spend against an annual target of 45%

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Smart ID and bank-branch channel
milestone: One million served at 669 bank branches, 2026-10-26
position_end: Smart ID replacements at 669 bank branches, used by 1,002,773 people since the first walk-in branch opened on 9 March 2026, on the department's figures of 26 October 2026, for 873 service points against 214 permanent offices; passport, first-time Smart ID and home-delivery services are to follow at more than 1,000 branches within months; green ID book production ends on 31 March 2027 and its recognition as identification is to be withdrawn by 31 March 2028; the department also commits to modernising 75 of the 145 remaining unmodernised local offices this financial year
note: the branch counts do not form a series - 372 and 408 one week apart in August, then 410 as at 13 August in a parliamentary reply, more than 500 by bank on 27 September, more than 515 on 1 October and 669 on 26 October; the October count does not name the participating banks

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Smart IDs issued, calendar year
position_end: Over four million smart identity documents issued in 2025/26, the highest annual output recorded
sources: 2026-05-15-dha-highest-ever-smart-id-output-2025-26|2026-01-28 Home Affairs sets new record by delivering over four million Smart IDs in 2025

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Social security agency messaging self-service channel
milestone: Modernisation programme set out at a media engagement, 17 September 2026
position_end: A messaging self-service channel letting a grant beneficiary check application, review and proof-of-life status without visiting an office, now set inside a wider modernisation programme: online applications, payment-detail changes and electronic life certification, self-service kiosks at offices with more advanced kiosks planned for strategic locations, free Wi-Fi at offices, and integration of the agency's information systems with other government institutions, which the agency says will help detect fraud and speed processing
note: the agency frames it as paying the right grant to the right person at the right time and place, and as a way to cut queues at local offices; no usage figure is published

subject: dpi.govtech
name: State IT agency audit outcome
milestone: Unqualified opinion on 2025/26, stated in a ministerial reply to Parliament
position_end: Unqualified opinion on 2025/26, on the minister's written reply to Parliament, after a qualified opinion on 2024/25 and a disclaimer on 2023/24; the reply puts 117 e-services delivered through 35 digital products to more than 30 departments and entities, and 80.66% of procurement requests met within target time against 80%
note: the 2025/26 opinion rests on the minister's reply, whose date is not stated; the annual report carrying it is not held

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Structural review to repurpose the State IT Agency
milestone: Review formally begun, stated by the minister at GovTech 2026
position_end: The communications department has formally begun a structural review to settle what the agency should be responsible for without being bogged down by procurement, the minister said at GovTech 2026; the managing director set out a shift from custom development to shared multi-tenant platforms and the retirement of legacy systems; no terms of reference, timetable or legislative vehicle is published

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Student-aid scheme systems integration
milestone: Public Protector gave the board 30 days to produce a plan, report released 2026-08-18
position_end: The Public Protector found the scheme's systems insufficiently integrated with the home affairs, social security and revenue data sources it needs to verify students, and directed a digital modernisation and systems-integration plan within 30 days covering institutional integration, verification interfaces, fraud controls and cyber security, elimination of duplicate applications and manual workarounds, student-facing case tracking and costed milestones
note: the report draws on a 2023 investigation finding some 40,000 non-qualifying students funded to more than R5.1bn, and records that the scheme cannot resolve 80% of contact-centre queries without internal escalation

subject: dpi.govtech
name: VAT modernisation consultation paper
position_end: The revenue service released a VAT Modernisation Consultation Paper proposing a digital VAT model combining electronic invoicing, an interoperability framework and electronic reporting, aimed at moving VAT administration off manual processes and retrospective verification and into the systems businesses already run; it follows a 2023 discussion paper and is stated as building blocks rather than a decided design
note: a consultation paper: no closing date for comment, implementation timetable, cost, mandate threshold or legislative vehicle is stated in the account held

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Western Cape e-Procurement Solution
position_end: The provincial government's e-procurement system, in use since 1999, processed 41,180 requests for quotation in 2024/25, with 21,404 awarded or finalised

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Western Cape funding-matching platform for small business
position_end: Free access for micro, small and medium enterprises in the province to a matching platform covering over 300 funders and 600 finance products
note: the platform is a private one and the funder and product counts are its own; the same data put 65.3% of provincial applicants as unable to supply their latest financial statements

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Western Cape Infrastructure Virtual Platform (EVE AI agent)
milestone: Launched at inaugural Infrastructure Ministerial Roundtable, 2026-07-30
position_end: Automatically evaluates projects against Treasury rules and ISO 9001 via AI agent EVE; evaluated pipeline of 52 projects worth R132bn, 11 worth over R20bn to be released to market; MoUs signed with Infrastructure South Africa, IFISA, EDC South Africa and UCT

subject: digital.localgov
name: City Power prepaid purchase monitoring platform
position_end: Johannesburg's power utility advertised a tender for near-real-time monitoring of prepaid purchases, revenue protection and metering support, permitting AI for anomaly detection on condition that outputs are explainable, auditable and POPIA-compliant, against R3.96bn of non-technical losses in 2024/25
note: no award or contract value is held

subject: digital.localgov
name: Emfuleni electronic records management system
milestone: Award recorded in quarterly procurement reporting
position_end: An in-house server-based electronic records-management system awarded on a three-year term from October 2025, recorded in the municipality's quarterly procurement report
note: known only through a procurement annexure, so the award is established and the deployment is not

subject: digital.localgov
name: Gauteng e-Government delivery
milestone: 2025/26 annual report presented to the provincial legislature
position_end: The provincial department reports 96 public Wi-Fi hotspots rolled out at schools, libraries, hospitals, clinics, hostels and licence testing centres offering up to 500MB of free internet a day, 33 e-services live, 99% provincial network uptime and 7,271 surveillance cameras on the provincial safety network, for 2025/26 (2026-09)
note: the department's own annual report as presented, with no audited outturn, usage figure or prior-year comparison in the account held

subject: digital.localgov
name: Home Affairs offices inside municipal buildings
position_end: An appointment-only office opened inside the Cape Town Civic Centre on 24 August 2026, which the city describes as the first municipal facility to host a national home affairs office; 148 people applied for services on the opening day, and the office is positioned to relieve the department's central business district office. Atlantis is named as the next priority in the city
note: the minister frames it as part of a strategy to decentralise access across bank branches, malls, smartphones and municipal buildings rather than concentrate it in departmental offices

subject: digital.localgov
name: Johannesburg free public Wi-Fi network (Metropolitan Tech Company)
milestone: 2026/27 business plan target of 200,000 connections, reported 2026-09-20
position_end: The city-owned company running the network recorded 1,574,979 free Wi-Fi connections in 2024/25 and its 2026/27 business plan targets 200,000, without explanation; it describes itself as under-capacitated, with 26 network-operations staff for 1,200km of fibre and R20.7m of capital budget against about R570m operating for 2026/27. Residents of the Slovo Park smart Wi-Fi pilot launched in March 2026 report very poor signal
note: the business plan as reported by a newspaper; the plan itself is not held

subject: digital.localgov
name: Mangaung metro records digitisation
milestone: Programme status reported to the NCOP
position_end: An information and communications technology roadmap, a document-management rollout and digitisation of hard-copy and historical municipal records reported to the National Council of Provinces, with budget, legacy-system and skills constraints named
note: the metro names its own constraints, which is rarer on this ledger than the programme itself

subject: digital.localgov
name: Municipal financial systems under the mSCOA standard
milestone: Treasury's state of local government finances report, 2026
position_end: The Treasury's 2026 report on local government finances finds councils still reporting from spreadsheets and ICT unfit for the standard chart of accounts; its 2024/25 budget circular required reporting only from the core financial system and quarterly valuation-roll reconciliation, and a 2020 parliamentary reply named councils budgeting in spreadsheets outside their core systems

subject: digital.localgov
name: Municipal revenue management plan
position_end: The local government association has issued a request for proposal for consultants to build a plan covering credible billing systems, collection strategies, recovery of long-outstanding debt and indigent management across the 257 municipalities it represents. The request puts municipal consumer debt at about R467.2bn and municipalities' own debt to creditors at about R160.8bn, states that many municipalities collect less than 70 per cent of billed revenue, and attributes about R25bn of annual water and electricity revenue loss to leaks, theft, illegal connections, inaccurate or outdated meters and weaknesses in metering and billing systems
note: unverified indigent registers and data deficiencies are named among the losses the consultants are to identify and quantify; no award, budget or timetable is stated

subject: digital.localgov
name: National archives guidance on managing electronic records
position_end: Standing guidance from the national archives on managing electronic records, the rule set the municipal digitisation programmes on this ledger are obliged to work to
note: an undated guidance page; no compliance assessment against it appears for any municipality

subject: digital.localgov
name: Provincial camera estate and its use by police
milestone: Camera networks offered to a police investigation, 17 September 2026
position_end: The provincial e-government department had access to 7,271 privately operated cameras in 2025/26 and a cumulative 960 of its own across townships, business districts, crime hotspots, major roads and schools, and is reported to have spent R124 million on closed-circuit television. It has offered the networks to a police investigation into nine women's bodies found since July 2026, for crime detection, investigation and intelligence gathering
note: no access rule, retention period, warrant requirement or audit of use is published for either the department's own cameras or the private network it reaches

subject: digital.localgov
name: Tshwane Enterprise Data and Analytics Platform
position_end: Pools municipal departments' service-delivery data in one system built with the CSIR, replacing static slides at weekly performance meetings; the live war-room dashboard stays internal, with a public dashboard to be considered only once the data is fully tested; a project collaboration agreement signed in August 2026 sets a two-year implementation period from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2028 with the city as pilot municipality, following a memorandum of June 2023; the city says the capability will extend across its seven regions, with ward councillors given access by mobile phone and each department naming a data custodian
note: no cost, budget or public release date stated

subject: digital.rural
name: Deeds registry service continuity after fire
milestone: Service moved to a new location
position_start: Did not exist as a recorded event
position_end: All paper records of registered land at one regional deeds registry already back-scanned into the electronic deeds system when the building burned, carrying service continuity to a new location
note: the clearest evidence on this ledger that back-scanning of a regional registry had actually been completed, and it is evidenced by a fire

subject: digital.rural
name: Electronic medical record implementation in eight provinces
position_end: Public-health service providers invited to implement the electronic medical record solution across eight provinces, with a provincial deployment already recognised in the Free State where training, connectivity, cybersecurity and interoperability are recorded as outstanding
note: the bid is held as an excerpt and no award, value or facility count is on file

subject: digital.rural
name: Integrated person management at police stations
milestone: Site count given to Parliament at 31 March 2026
position_start: Did not exist on the repository
position_end: The count of police sites with integrated person management implemented given to Parliament as at 31 March 2026, with personnel, connectivity, rugged devices and scanners named as the dependencies for wider rollout, alongside station hardware and network rollout counts and an electronic policing policy directing digital docket management into pilot stations
note: the dependencies named are physical rather than software, which is what makes rural rollout the binding case

subject: digital.rural
name: KwaZulu-Natal Digital Access Programme
milestone: Launched at a rural primary school
position_end: A provincial treasury programme for rural and under-resourced schools launched in one district, with announced expansion to two further districts
note: no school count, budget or device figure is published; the national digital education strategy of September 2025 is the policy frame it sits under

subject: digital.rural
name: Off-grid school media lab
position_end: A containerised off-grid media lab in service at one primary school, with solar generation and battery storage, offering coding and robotics training to surrounding schools
note: one site; the off-grid design is the notable part, against the rural electrification position reported on this ledger

subject: tech.ai
name: AI Maturity Matrix archetype
position_end: Gradual Practitioner, one of 21 economies in that archetype of the consultancy's matrix (October 2026)
note: a consultancy's classification of more than 75 economies

subject: tech.ai
name: AI use in the financial sector
movement: No change, a first count with no earlier figure behind it
position_end: 220 of about 2,100 surveyed financial firms, 10.6%, use AI, banks leading at about 52% (survey launched October 2024)
note: the conduct and prudential regulators' own survey

subject: tech.ai
name: Appeal on algorithmic eligibility verification for the SRD grant
milestone: Argued before the Supreme Court of Appeal 2026-08-25
position_end: the state's appeal against the January 2025 high court ruling on the online-only relief grant argued in Bloemfontein on 25 August 2026, with judgment reserved pending further affidavits
note: this is the closest thing the record holds to a rule on state automated decision-making, and it is litigation rather than an instrument; no judgment in the appeal is on file and the row governing rules for state automated decision-making remains Not held

subject: tech.ai
name: Artificial-intelligence startups counted in a continental census
position_start: Not held: the deposit's 2022 and 2025 editions are not held, so the repository carries no count before this one
position_end: 49 firms located in the country in the 2026 edition of the census, out of 224 across 22 countries and a Pan-African category, founded 2002 to 2025
note: a third-party census compiled from public sources, not an official register; no change over time can be stated while the earlier editions are unheld

subject: tech.ai
name: Automated selection at SARS
position_end: 100% of verifications, 88.41% of complex audits

subject: tech.ai
name: Centre for Artificial Intelligence Research
position_end: A distributed national research network in artificial intelligence hosted across universities with a national coordinating centre, the country's standing public research capability in the field
note: an undated institutional page carrying no funding, headcount or output figure; the comparative study of national strategies places the country's policy position rather than its research base

subject: tech.ai
name: Companies registry AI transactional chatbot
position_end: Open tender for an AI-powered multi-channel transactional chatbot for the companies and intellectual property commission, closing 6 February 2026; no award is reported

subject: tech.ai
name: Country-hosted AI compute (UNDP AI Infrastructure Activation)
milestone: Funder's lessons from the six-country deployment published 17 September 2026
position_end: GPU capacity procured, installed and activated with public institutions under a UNDP programme in six countries, the higher-specification training capacity concentrated in Kenya and South Africa; its priority use, crop observation from satellite and agricultural research data, waits on clearer access to data held across institutions
note: the funder's own account; no capacity figure, host site or deployment date is stated

subject: tech.ai
name: Customer-facing AI assistant at a major bank
position_end: An agentic artificial-intelligence chatbot handling over 100,000 queries a month from about 1.6 million users in the first half of 2026, alongside 30,000 employees a month on a vendor productivity assistant, more than 3,800 staff-built automation agents in production and over 1,400 developers on AI-assisted coding tools
note: the bank's own figures, reported at interim results; a different institution from the enterprise-adoption row above and not comparable with it

subject: tech.ai
name: Employees bypassing workplace AI restrictions
position_end: Half of 903 South Africans surveyed had bypassed an employer's restrictions on AI tools in the past year and 35% had seen AI-generated work passed off as human, on a consultancy partner's account of a survey report due in November 2026; consumer trust in AI rose from 11% in 2023 to 44% in 2026
note: stated at a roundtable ahead of publication; the report is not held

subject: tech.ai
name: Enterprise AI adoption at a major bank
position_end: More than 39,000 staff, 72% of the workforce, reported as active generative-artificial-intelligence users on a multi-model enterprise platform hosted on a foreign cloud provider, with relationship management, servicing, payments and lending named as the four priority areas
note: the bank's own figures for active users, not for automated decisions or customer-facing deployment; no model inventory, assurance process or customer disclosure is stated, and the country holds no artificial-intelligence incident or assurance register

subject: tech.ai
name: Film and Publication Board digitisation and AI strategy
milestone: Approval reported by the acting chief executive, 2026-09-21
position_end: Approved and built into the board's 2025-2030 strategic plan with quarterly monitoring; generative AI for content monitoring, classification and case management is to be explored over three to five years and none is yet in use, while keyword-crawling monitoring tools and a WhatsApp reporting line already run

subject: tech.ai
name: Four-university African-language AI consortium
position_end: Four universities, led from Zululand, building AI tools and language models for isiXhosa, isiZulu and Sepedi with research-foundation and telecoms-operator centre-of-excellence funding

subject: tech.ai
name: FSCA responsible AI framework
milestone: Stated in development in the 2025/26 integrated report, presented to Parliament's finance committee in the week of 2026-09-30
position_end: A framework to guide the conduct regulator's own development and deployment of AI, the only outstanding element under its governance principle on data, information and technology
note: a framework for the regulator's own use of AI, not a rule for supervised firms; no publication date stated

subject: tech.ai
name: HPCSA ethical guidelines on the use of AI (Booklet 20)
position_end: The health professions council's guidelines set disclosure, accountability, consent and data-protection duties for practitioners using AI, with devices left to the medicines regulator's rules
note: an earlier September 2024 edition circulates separately

subject: tech.ai
name: Institutional policy on artificial intelligence in higher education
milestone: Absence set out in university research presented 2026-08-17
position_end: Not held
note: research from a South African university finds artificial-intelligence adoption in teaching and assessment outpacing institutional policy, with lecturers reporting inconsistent or absent guidance on accountability, the reliability of detection tools and academic integrity; no sector-wide instrument or regulator guidance is held

subject: tech.ai
name: Lwazi, the SARS AI assistant
milestone: More than 2.7 million questions answered in 2025/26
position_end: The revenue service's AI assistant answered more than 2.7 million taxpayer questions in 2025/26

subject: tech.ai
name: Machine-learning screening of travellers for fraud
position_end: Stated intention to screen travellers for fraud using machine learning; no system, procurement, legal basis, accuracy measure or appeal route is published
note: An intention reported in the trade press; no instrument establishes it.

subject: tech.ai
name: Mzansi Mind and the Siya language model
milestone: Hardware selection announced by the vendor 2026-10-22
position_end: A private sovereign enterprise AI platform running its Siya model across all official languages, on HPE servers with NVIDIA GPUs at a Johannesburg colocation centre, citing data-residency requirements
note: a hardware vendor's release

subject: tech.ai
name: MzansiLM and the MzansiText corpus
position_end: An open decoder-only language model trained from scratch on a curated dataset covering all 11 official written languages, built at the University of Cape Town

subject: tech.ai
name: News websites blocking at least one AI crawler
milestone: Second country report of a three-country series, August 2026
position_start: 29.7% of the news websites surveyed disallowed at least one AI crawler (2025-12)
position_end: 30.4% of 263 news websites disallow at least one AI crawler in their robots.txt file, of which 195 (74.1%) carry a robots.txt file at all (2026-04)
note: robots.txt is a request, not an access control, so the figure measures stated intent rather than crawling that was prevented

subject: tech.ai
name: openScopes AIDDiA AI microscopy programme
position_end: A four-year programme led by the University of Cape Town and funded by the Wellcome Trust at GBP 4.4m (about R101m), combining open-source microscopy with machine-learning image analysis for infectious-disease research, with partners in Kenya, Uganda and Cote d'Ivoire; locally repairable microscopes are to be installed at four African partner institutions

subject: tech.ai
name: Operator use of AI for revenue assurance
milestone: Stated in use against zero-rating tunnelling, 2026-09-10
position_start: Not previously held by this repository
position_end: The largest mobile operator is using artificial intelligence for revenue assurance, identifying leakage where fraudsters use tunnelling to redirect traffic through zero-rated sites such as university websites, its chief executive said in an account reported 10 September 2026; he said adoption has accelerated as practical applications emerge across the business. Zero-rating here dates from the COVID-19 response, when the communications regulator acted to make educational and public-interest sites free to reach.
note: the operator's own account with no measured leakage, recovery figure or detection rate published, and no regulator statement on the abuse of zero-rated routes is held

subject: tech.ai
name: Placing on the Africa AI Governance Index
position_end: Eleventh in Africa on capacity to govern artificial intelligence, scoring 2.10 of four against Rwanda on 3.25, Nigeria on 2.81 and Benin on 2.58, the three states the index classifies as having established AI governance
note: the index is the Lawyers Hub's, published July 2026 across eight weighted pillars and 80 indicators per country; earlier editions are not held

subject: tech.ai
name: Police impersonation offence applied to AI-generated images
position_end: Provincial police have warned the public that creating and sharing artificial-intelligence face-swap images of themselves in police uniform can breach section 68 of the South African Police Service Act 68 of 1995, which makes impersonating a police official an offence: an existing statute asserted against a new practice rather than a new rule (2026-09)
note: a provincial warning, not a national directive or a prosecution: no case, charge or takedown route is published

subject: tech.ai
name: Proposed AI regulatory institutions
position_end: Under reconsideration; committee opposed

subject: tech.ai
name: Prudential Authority AI and cloud supervision standards

subject: tech.ai

position_end: None

subject: tech.ai
name: SAHPRA AI/ML medical-device requirements
position_end: Issued 2025-09-26; product registration not commenced
note: Communication to Stakeholders MD08-2025/2026: every AI/ML-enabled medical device or IVD must be authorised before use and its importer or manufacturer licensed under s.22C of Act 101 of 1965, with Class C and D applicants required to produce prior approval from one of six reference jurisdictions or WHO prequalification and local clinical evidence including subgroup analysis by sex, age and ethnicity; ISO 13485:2016, IEC 62304 and POPIA apply; SAHPRA states it has not commenced product registration of medical devices under regulation 8, that AI-specific pathways are still to be developed and that it awaits IMDRF guidance before adopting predetermined change control plans

subject: tech.ai
name: SARS AI-driven digital twin
position_end: Request for information on an AI-driven digital twin for cognitive decision automation at the revenue service; no tender or award is reported

subject: tech.ai
name: SARS Modernisation 3.0
milestone: Commissioner set out the programme at the 13th Tax Indaba, 2026-09-14
position_start: Announced 2026-04, reaching the repository only through a trade-press account
position_end: The revenue service has now published its own account of the programme: the commissioner's keynote of 14 September 2026 puts trust, institutional capability, modernisation and stakeholder partnership at the centre of compliance strategy, following a stakeholder-listening exercise in his first months in office. No delivery dates, budget or system scope are stated
sources: 2026-09-14-zaf-sars-modernisation-3-0-tax-administration-vision|2026-04-03 Say goodbye to SARS tax numbers in South Africa
note: a strategy statement, not a delivery milestone: nothing is dated, costed or scoped

subject: tech.ai
name: Standard Bank Responsible AI Approach
position_end: A framework for developing, deploying and using AI with human oversight and accountability across the system life cycle, produced with a university data-science school and presented as usable by any business
note: a private framework with no regulatory standing; no audit, disclosure or enforcement mechanism is stated

subject: tech.ai
name: Start-up funding, South Africa
position_start: Led Africa on equity and deal count, CY2025
position_end: Fourth at $83m, H1 2026

subject: tech.ai
name: State airports company Airport 4.0 programme
milestone: Set out in the annual report released 2026-09-14
position_end: A five-year plan to 2031 to bring AI, connected sensors, blockchain and robotics into airport operations, including AI at check-in, security, baggage handling and parking, terminal patrol robots and a first-year proof of concept for a metaverse platform, inside a R21.7bn capital investment pipeline covering digitisation and infrastructure modernisation (2026-09)
note: the R21.7bn pipeline is not broken down, so no sum is attributable to the digital components; cyber attacks are listed among the risks the plan addresses

subject: tech.ai
name: State funding of language resources and the absence of a state language model
milestone: Minister's written reply to Parliament, October 2025
position_end: The science department funds human-language-technology research at the CSIR, since 2006, and the national centre for digital language resources at North-West University, which distributes resources in all official languages free for research; the minister stated that no government-backed home-grown large language model is under development

subject: tech.ai
name: State insurer national risk forecasting
position_end: The state-owned special-risks insurer uses artificial intelligence, behavioural signals and social science to identify the conditions that precede national disasters
note: the account is the insurer's own; no model, accuracy measure, decision it feeds or governance arrangement is stated

subject: tech.ai
name: State of AI Policy in Africa score
position_end: 19 of 24 on a twelve-criterion rubric of policy design and delivery, the framework counted as a draft (October 2025)
note: a private analysts' index; earlier editions are not held

subject: tech.ai
name: Western Cape AI Cluster and its responsible-AI programme
milestone: Programme announced 17 August 2026, first summit 25 August 2026
position_end: A responsible-AI programme announced on 17 August 2026 under a newly created provincial AI cluster, run with the provincial economic development department, whose first summit at Cape Town on 25 August 2026 covered AI policy, governance, infrastructure investment and sovereign AI; it was convened after the national department withdrew the draft national AI policy
note: a provincial and industry-association initiative, with no budget or work programme stated

subject: tech.industry
name: B-BBEE ICT Sector Council
status: Implemented, chair replaced on an interim basis
milestone: Interim chair appointed for six months, reported 2026-08-14
position_end: The communications minister replaced the council’s chairperson and appointed an interim chair for six months after a departmental investigation found the council dysfunctional; the investigation report is not published, and no remedial plan, terms of reference for the interim period or date for a permanent appointment is stated

subject: tech.industry
name: Bank-operated mobile virtual network
milestone: Latest full-year figures given by the operator
position_end: R28.6bn of customer value and sales, R3bn of gross revenue, about 50 petabytes of data carried and 1.02 million subscriber identities
note: The operator's own figures; no regulator series covers virtual network scale

subject: tech.industry
name: Cell C financial turnaround
milestone: R4.9bn write-down of the stake by its listed holder
position_end: Its listed holder booked a R4.9 billion full-year loss writing the stake down to the operator's R9 billion listing price and now holds 49.53% of it, with net income 297% down year on year on the write-down alone
note: an asset-light model on other operators' radio networks, so the wholesale growth is a virtual-operator business rather than network build

subject: tech.industry
name: Cross-border e-commerce growth after the small-parcel concession ended
position_end: Growth in cross-border e-commerce significantly slowed by the crackdown on low-value imports, with the two largest platforms shifting from tax arbitrage towards local fulfilment and supply chains, on the Online Retail in South Africa study
note: the coincidence of the tax change and the slowdown is the study's framing rather than a tested causal claim; both platforms have since moved toward locally compliant supply chains and local merchant programmes

subject: tech.industry
name: E-hailing operating licence regime
milestone: Western Cape undertook to add e-hailing to its licence application, 21 August 2026
position_start: A national registration regime under the National Land Transport Amendment Act, 2023 and the Second National Land Transport Regulations, 2025, with provincial application forms not yet carrying e-hailing as a service option
position_end: A platform carried its compliance programme into the provinces — a North West regulatory engagement in Rustenburg on 18 August 2026 attended by more than 150 operators, and a Western Cape transport dialogue in Cape Town on 21 August at which the provincial mobility department's director of licensing and adjudication undertook to add e-hailing as a service option on the operating-licence application; the North West provincial regulatory entity put its pending operating-licence backlog at 3,000 to 5,000 applications
note: the account is the platform's own and the undertaking is not yet an amended form; the platform states it was among the first to receive a Certificate of Registration from the national regulator, in February 2026

subject: tech.industry
name: Informal-retail transaction data product
milestone: Rebranded into a consolidated merchant division 2026-08-19
position_end: A listed payments company sells near-real-time item-level intelligence on the informal retail economy, drawn from a point-of-sale network of over 90,000 spaza shops and taverns and 10,500 checkouts, to consumer-goods brands, wholesalers and financiers
note: the network figures are the company's own; no consent basis, pricing or data-protection assessment for the resale of merchant transaction data is stated

subject: tech.industry
name: Mobile virtual network operator subscriptions
milestone: Operator results for the 12 months to 2026-05-31, presented 2026-08-21
position_end: About 4.4 million active MVNO SIMs at end-2025 on an analyst count, up about 43% year on year and forecast to reach 14.4 million by 2030; the fourth-largest of the five mobile operators reported 5.7 million MVNO subscribers carried on its own wholesale platform for the 12 months to 2026-05-31, which it put at an estimated 80-85% share of the market
note: two different bases, not a series: the 4.4 million is an analyst house's count of active SIMs at end-2025 with no published methodology, and the 5.7 million is one operator's own count of subscribers on its wholesale platform to 2026-05-31. The analyst report puts South Africa first on the continent and forecasts that South Africa, Nigeria, Kenya and Uganda together will hold 85% of Africa's 39.6 million MVNO subscribers by 2030

subject: tech.industry
name: Online retail as a share of national retail turnover
milestone: Crossed 10 per cent of national retail turnover in June 2026
position_end: Above 10 per cent of national retail turnover from June 2026 and forecast at ZAR 159 billion for the year, growth of 22.5 per cent, on the study's own publisher rather than a trade-press account, with retailer-level results and platform and payment detail (2026-09)
note: An industry study; the year-on-year increase of about ZAR 29 billion is close to the whole of the 2020 online retail market.

subject: tech.industry
name: Platform programme for news creators
position_end: Eight South African news creators joined a technology company's growth programme for independent news publishers
note: a company programme with eight named places, running against the same company's market-inquiry findings and remedy that this repository records separately

subject: tech.industry
name: Proposed Octotel and MetroFibre merger
position_end: Their common owner, which holds all of Octotel and 37% of MetroFibre, is assessing a combination that would form the third-largest fibre network behind Vumatel and Openserve; nothing finalised
note: the report relies on other outlets for the companies' statements

subject: tech.industry
name: Standard Bank investment in OPay
position_end: The largest African bank by assets signed a subscription agreement to invest in a digital financial platform operating mainly in Nigeria, to close with or shortly after the platform's proposed New York listing and subject to regulatory approvals; the two intend to explore digital banking, merchant acquiring, payments, lending and remittances across African markets; no amount is stated

subject: tech.industry
name: The largest domestic operator's interest in the Kenyan incumbent
status: Implemented, voided by a foreign court and under appeal
milestone: Kenyan High Court voided the underlying sale, 15 September 2026
position_end: The group bought out its parent's remaining 12.5 per cent of the Kenyan holding company on 30 June 2026, lifting its effective interest in the Kenyan incumbent from 35 to 55 per cent on the same day the Kenyan state sold a 15 per cent stake. A three-judge bench has voided that sale as unconstitutional and ordered the shares back to the state, so the enlarged interest rests on a transaction now under appeal
note: the ruling is a Kenyan court's; what it settles for the South African group's consolidated position is not stated anywhere on the record

subject: tech.innovate
name: African Digital Transformation Centre
milestone: Opened at The Innovation Hub, Pretoria
position_end: Opened with the International Telecommunication Union as part of its network of acceleration centres, to support information and communications technology small enterprises and digital entrepreneurs across the continent
note: no tenancy, cohort or funding figure is published

subject: tech.innovate
name: Alpha Ticker
note: a newly launched vehicle whose three stated arms are capital deployment, an artificial-intelligence decision-intelligence product for portfolio analysis, and Compute Africa, which targets data-centre, energy and connectivity infrastructure in sub-Saharan Africa; no fund size, capital raised, investment made or timetable is published, and the account is a founder profile rather than a company filing

subject: tech.innovate
name: Domestic scale-up fund

note: a launch rather than a deployment; no first investment, sector focus or ticket size is published

subject: tech.innovate
name: Google for Startups Accelerator: South Africa, 2026 cohort
position_end: Fifteen South African-led, revenue-generating AI startups were named to a three-month programme running to a December demo day, each offered up to R1m in equity-free funding with the company's AI models, cloud and mentorship

subject: tech.innovate
name: Injini Southern Africa AI edtech programme

subject: tech.innovate

subject: tech.innovate

subject: tech.innovate

position_end: First close at R300 million (US$18.8 million) against a R550 million (US$34.4 million) target, anchored by the state asset manager, to invest in post-revenue South African technology companies

subject: tech.innovate
name: Small business incubation and digital hubs

note: no programme, budget or occupancy is published; it is the second hub opened in the window

subject: tech.innovate
name: Start-up funding conditions
milestone: Recovery reported alongside a persistent fit problem
position_end: Recovering, with founders reported as still unable to find capital matched to their stage even where they have customers and revenue (2026-09)
note: No aggregate funding figure is given in the account.

subject: capacity.literacy
