note: held as an excerpt and two years old at the window's close; no digital-literacy or digital-skills rate is measured in it or anywhere else on this ledger

subject: capacity.literacy
name: National School of Government digital skills for public servants
position_end: The school trained 112,855 learners in 2024/25 and runs a Microsoft agreement to train 100,000 public servants in digital literacy, AI and cybersecurity; 4,725 had completed its free online courses in AI fluency, cyber awareness and mobile literacy by August 2025

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Western Cape eCentre network
position_start: The network operating with no count on the repository
position_end: The 83rd brick-and-mortar eCentre opened, adding a business corner, public access centre and training centre to a network also served by a mobile eCentre
note: a provincial network; no user, training or throughput figure is published for it

subject: capacity.training
name: Coding and Robotics curriculum in public schools
milestone: Introduction in public schools reported August 2026
position_end: Introduced in public schools, covering digital literacy, coding, artificial intelligence and robotics, with the basic education department training teachers
note: the one record gives no rollout date, grade coverage or school count, and has no publisher URL

subject: capacity.training
name: Data-centre operations academy
milestone: Two domestic firms joined and funded a full 2026 cohort
position_start: An academy without industry-funded places at cohort scale
position_end: Two domestic firms joined as industry partners and are sponsoring a full candidate cohort for the 2026 intake, the first South African firms to fund a whole cohort, one opening a newly launched Midrand OEM training facility and the other a live operational data centre to supply the practical component of a graduate-to-employment pipeline its founder frames as a recruitment expense rather than a training one
note: no cohort size, placement rate or cost per place is published

subject: capacity.training
name: Digital Skills Impact Fund
position_start: A R200m fund open through fixed application windows
position_end: R600m mobilised from 600 organisations and 4,000 young people reached, with 95% of completers of its work-based programmes absorbed into employment; the coordinating body seeks a further R2.5bn from existing state skills funds for 20,000 more by 2028, not yet committed, against a target of 500,000 young people into digital roles by 2034

subject: capacity.training
name: Digital-skills pipeline from school to employment
milestone: Reviewed in a report with the higher education department, 2026-08-14
position_end: Constrained at both ends and worsening on the employers' own account: a university survey reports about 55% of businesses saying workers show little or no proficiency in mathematics or data skills, 55% saying their workforce has only basic digital literacy, 52% finding it difficult to hire people prepared for digital transformation and 70% rating their workforce's technology skills poor or very poor, against 118,500 unfilled ICT vacancies of which 36% are junior roles; the country is placed second in the world on education spending and 67th on digital skills (2026-09)
note: the figures reach the repository through an industry opinion piece citing a university survey and a non-profit's vacancy count; neither underlying dataset is held, and the ranking pair is quoted without its source index

subject: capacity.training
name: Huawei and National School of Government digital skills MOU
position_end: A two-year agreement to put selected Huawei courses in AI, cyber security, networking, storage, cloud and digital government on the school's U-Learning platform for public servants

subject: capacity.training
name: ICT devices and connectivity in public schools
position_end: 535,673 learners and 10,054 classrooms were given ICT devices from 2022/23 to 2024/25, and connectivity was provided to 17,164 schools

subject: capacity.training
name: Industry Connect ICT jobs portal
milestone: Portal launched by the ICT industry association, 2026-08-28
position_end: A portal launched by the ICT industry association to link employers, ICT jobseekers and graduates and professional development in one platform rather than as a conventional job board, its stated purpose being the disconnect between people holding ICT skills and the businesses that need them; it arrives as government and business enter the third phase of a partnership to create a million jobs by 2030. No listing count, placement figure, funding or operator arrangement is published
note: an association's own launch announcement carried in a trade account; nothing establishes whether any employer or jobseeker is yet on it

subject: capacity.training
name: National Digital and Future Skills Strategy 2020
position_end: Under review; no replacement
note: the 2020 strategy is under comprehensive review, disclosed in a written parliamentary reply rather than announced; DCDT declined to forecast AI's net employment effect, holding that it depends on the country's ability to equip workers

subject: capacity.training
name: Provincial low-code skills transfer programme
milestone: Three-day programme for 20 provincial IT specialists
position_end: A three-day skills-transfer programme run by a vendor and an implementation partner for 20 IT specialists of a provincial department (2026-09)
note: The implementation partner's own recommendation is that the department build on it with a provincial programme; none is announced.

subject: capacity.training
name: Public schools with a computer centre
position_end: 34.1% of 22,511 public schools have a computer centre, 11.6% in the Eastern Cape (2024)

subject: capacity.training
name: Public-sector cloud and cybersecurity upskilling programme with Google
milestone: Launched by the public service minister 2024-11-05
position_end: Launched to equip 13,000 South Africans with advanced cybersecurity skills between November 2024 and November 2025; the minister put the public service's ICT staff at about 4,500 of 1.2 million public servants
note: the minister's launch speech; no completion figure is held

subject: capacity.training
name: Vendor digital-skills programme in Northern Cape schools
milestone: Partnership announced 2026-08-18 for classes from February 2027
position_end: A networking vendor's academy and a private group agreed with the provincial education department to take networking, cyber security and artificial-intelligence courses into 235 schools, as extracurricular classes for grades 10 to 12 beginning February 2027, inside a global skills-to-jobs programme the vendor states has trained more than 600,000 South Africans
note: announced for a start five months away; no learner target, cost, funding split, teacher-training provision or certification pathway is published, and the 600,000 figure is the vendor's own

subject: capacity.research
name: Standing in digital-privacy research
position_end: 18th worldwide and the only African country in the top 20 for digital-privacy research output, on a 4,760-article review of 2005-2025
note: a bibliometric analysis of 4,760 Scopus and Web of Science articles over twenty years, published in a South African journal; the same review finds refugees, people with disabilities, older people and racial and ethnic minorities notably underrepresented in the literature, so the ranking measures volume of output and not coverage of the populations most exposed

subject: include.access
name: Bank self-service kiosk network
position_end: 581 self-service kiosks handling more than half a million transactions a month across over 60 banking services, through which almost 70% of instant-issued debit cards are dispensed and 56% of kiosk-issued cards go to entry-level clients; mall-based zones pairing kiosks with consultant support enter pilot at a Johannesburg mall in late August 2026, with wider deployment flagged for the mid- to long term
note: one bank's own figures; no regulator series covers self-service banking channels

subject: include.access
name: Bank-account means test across eight grants
position_end: Undecided; SCA hearing 2026-08-25

subject: include.access
name: DCDT expenditure
position_end: R3.61bn of R3.74bn spent, FY2025/26

subject: include.access
name: Disability-inclusive data cooperation with China
position_end: A seven-point plan agreed to deepen cooperation on disability-inclusive data, universal design and artificial-intelligence-enabled assistive technology, anchored in a proposed disability centre of excellence working with the national statistics office
note: no instrument, funding, timetable or data-sharing arrangement is published for cooperation that names a national statistics office as a partner

subject: include.access
name: Employment Services Amendment Bill
position_end: Published, extending the statutory employment-services framework to foreign nationals, refugees and asylum seekers, creating work-authorisation verification and requiring a framework for collecting information on their recruitment and employment
note: the verification duty it creates would run against the population register; the 1998 refugees statute is the standing frame it amends around

subject: include.access
name: Grant payments to deceased beneficiaries
position_end: About R140m paid to some 75,000 dead beneficiaries in 2023/24, which the agency attributed to deaths during the payment cycle and late death registration with Home Affairs, with a bulk recall system stated as coming

subject: include.access
name: Internet prices against headline inflation
position_start: Wired internet up 18.6% and wireless up 6.4% over January 2020 to July 2026, against headline inflation of 36%
position_end: Wired internet up 3.5% and wireless up 4.1% over the first half of 2026, both ahead of cumulative headline inflation of 3.8% - a reversal of the six-year pattern in which both ran well below it, and the competition authority calls the recent trend concerning for a service it treats as essential (2026-07)
note: drawn from the statistics agency's consumer price index at the most disaggregated category capturing lower-income expenditure, so it tracks advertised basket prices rather than what any household pays

subject: include.access
name: Khawuleza app
milestone: Functionality problems reported to the NCOP, 2025-10
position_end: The Presidential Hotline's app, developed in-house, took no cases after a pilot in Limpopo failed on technical faults (December 2024), and its functionality problems were still unresolved in October 2025

subject: include.access
name: Legal framework for ICT access by persons with disabilities
position_end: Constitutional equality guarantees, the Equality Act and the Electronic Communications Act's universal-access duties cover ICT access for persons with disabilities, but there is no specific ICT-accessibility legislation and the Marrakesh Treaty has not been acceded to; accessible-format exceptions in copyright came through a Constitutional Court ruling

subject: include.access
name: MICT SETA
position_end: Referred for assessment 2026-07-21

subject: include.access
name: Mobile specialist referral platform, patients referred
movement: No change, a first count with no earlier figure behind it
position_end: More than three million patients referred to specialists through a mobile app linking rural health workers with specialist doctors, present in five southern African countries (2026-09)
note: a cumulative count across five countries, not split by country; the date the threshold was passed is not given

subject: include.access
name: Money Smart Week
position_end: a national financial-education week run from 24 to 30 August 2026 by the committee the Treasury and the conduct authority established to co-ordinate financial literacy

subject: include.access
name: Municipal citizen service application
position_end: A digital service-reporting channel letting residents log and track requests and receive municipal updates
note: one small municipality; no user or request figure is published

subject: include.access
name: National study on digital gender transformation
position_end: A national study announced by the gender equality commission on women's participation in the digital economy, aimed at producing gender-responsive policy recommendations to close the digital access gap
note: the standing instrument beside it is a gender-responsive planning and budgeting framework, which is a budgeting method rather than a digital measure

subject: include.access
name: ParliMeter parliamentary monitoring platform
milestone: Custodianship passed to the Parliamentary Monitoring Group, 2026-09-09
position_start: Running under an EU co-funded accountability project
position_end: Tracking MP attendance, the progress of bills, committee meetings, questions to ministers and their answers, and parliament's performance against democratic-parliament indicators, with custodianship passing to the Parliamentary Monitoring Group as the EU co-funded phase closes
note: a civil-society platform; no funding for the next phase or usage figure is published

subject: include.access
name: Postbank Black Card migration
position_end: 172,146 replaced by 2026-07-28; 264,263 outstanding
note: of 463,836 active gold cards at 2026-04-29, 172,146 had been replaced by 2026-07-28, 8,119 subsequently dropped off the SASSA file and 264,263 remain, roughly 40% of them in KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng and 43,515 in the Western Cape; Postbank reports 306 replacement sites against a target of 300 plus nine mobile teams, ring-fences customers more than 30km from a site, and plans the rollout from monthly SASSA data on the location of each customer's last three transactions

subject: include.access
name: Presidential Hotline
milestone: Oversight visit to its call centre, 2026-09-09
position_start: Operating since September 2009 as the apex government complaints channel
position_end: Operating since September 2009 as the apex channel for complaints, enquiries and suggestions on government services, escalating unresolved cases to departments on the state IT agency's case-management platform, under review for automation
note: case volume and resolution rate are carried on the resolution-rate measure row

subject: include.access
name: Presidential Hotline resolution rate
position_end: 59% of complaints resolved from April to October 2025, up from 40%, provinces at 63% and national departments at 58%; 339,579 cases logged since 2009, 96.7% of complaints resolved, reported December 2024

subject: include.access
name: Regulator market inquiry into the affordability of telecommunications services
status: In development, notice withdrawn for republication
milestone: Notice 4130 withdrawn by General Notice 4180, Gazette 55476, 2026-09-30
position_start: Gazetted on 4 September 2026 as a section 4B market inquiry in four phases
position_end: The regulator withdrew the inquiry notice on 30 September 2026, 26 days after gazetting it, to address administrative and procedural matters; it says the notice will be republished with a draft questionnaire for public comment, and that those who have already commented may resubmit. The same gazette prints a draft notice of intention to run the inquiry in four phases under section 4B
note: no republication date is given; the communications department is running a separate cost-to-communicate study in parallel

subject: include.access
name: Roads4U road-defect reporting application
position_end: A public road-defect reporting application that geolocates each report and routes it to the responsible road authority, issuing reference numbers and status updates to the reporter
note: the routing and the reference number are what distinguish it from a complaints inbox; no volume figure is published

subject: include.access
name: SASSA biometric verification against Home Affairs
milestone: R13.1bn saved, stated in the 2026 MTBPS documents
position_end: 997,379 of 19.05m recipients verified (2026-03); the Treasury credits biometric enrolment with R13.1bn saved, mostly on the relief grant, with student-aid and housing subsidies next and R6.2bn more expected by 2029/30

subject: include.access
name: SASSA grant reviews
milestone: Qualified audit for 2025/26 over payment-system weaknesses, heard 6 October 2026
position_end: The social security agency flagged more than 420,000 grant beneficiaries for review in 2025/26 and claims R1 billion saved, and aims to review up to 350,000 in 2026/27 for a further R1.5 billion, a saving the Treasury's 2026 Budget Review also carries. An investigative account finds the anti-fraud effort falls on beneficiaries rather than on the private firms deducting from grants, documenting a pensioner losing R205 a month, nearly a tenth of a R2,310 grant, to a funeral policy he did not consent to after people describing themselves as agency volunteers collected names, identity numbers and phone numbers; the social development department received a qualified audit opinion for 2025/26 over weaknesses in the agency's payment system, including grants paid to deceased people and government employees, heard by Parliament's committee on 6 October 2026; the agency defended its reviews, life certification and biometric enrolment as fraud controls on 9 October
note: the agency's contracts with commercial banks provide for means-test and fraud checks against credit bureaus and a fraud prevention service but carry no protection against recipients' data being used to market financial products

subject: include.access
name: SITA performance
position_end: The Public Service Commission's investigation of government IT procurement over 2020 to 2025 found executive leadership gaps among the root causes of instability at the agency, with 86% of managing-director roles held on an acting or interim basis and board tenures too short for strategic continuity, alongside irregular expenditure above R2bn across four audited years which it read as control failure through absent deterrence. A permanent managing director, the first since late 2023, took office in April 2026 as the minister constituted a new board; he describes the agency's standing with client departments as low and is moving it towards shared multi-tenant platforms. It supports more than 100 departments and public entities on annual billing of R7.4bn, and some client departments are looking for alternatives. Its managing director said in September 2026 that 60% of executive committee posts had been vacant and that a permanent chief financial officer and executives for client engagement, supply chain, and network, cloud and platform have since been appointed
sources: 2026-09-22-sita-recovery-mode-comms-minister|2026-09-21-zaf-businessday-sita-boss-rebuild-trust|2026-09-21-zaf-govza-malatsi-national-digital-sovereignty-agenda-govtech|2026-08-28-itwebza-sita-executive-recruitment-psc-report|2026-07-07 South Africa's state IT agency is slowing government tech rollout|2026-07-06-sita-r2bn-irregular-spending
note: the commission's report is summarised in a trade account of a committee sitting; the report itself is not held

subject: include.access
name: Smartphone excise removal
movement: Advanced, offset by rising device prices
position_end: 1.1m additional entry-level units, against a continental average selling price up $41 to $202 and sub-$100 shipments down 34% year on year in Q2 2026
sources: 2026-08-20-ai-driving-up-africa-smartphone-prices|2026-07-10 SOLLY MALATSI  Removing smartphone tax means access to opportunity
note: the excise removal of April 2025 is credited by the minister with 1.1m additional entry-level units; against it, Omdia reports African sub-$100 smartphone shipments down 34% year on year in Q2 2026 and the continental average selling price up $41 to $202, attributed to AI-driven memory and semiconductor demand - a tax cut and a component-cost rise working on the same price in opposite directions, and the repository holds no South-Africa-specific unit or price series to net them against

subject: include.divides
name: Adults shopping online
milestone: Online Retail in South Africa 2026 report, reported 2026-09-21
position_end: 34.2% of adults in 2025 against 79.1% of adults online; 23.9% among LSM 3 to 6 adults, of whom 70.4% are online, and 31.7% of women against 36.9% of men
note: an industry survey produced with a card scheme and a payment processor

subject: include.divides
name: Households with no telephone
position_start: nearly 55% of households with no telephone at all in 2002
position_end: 3.7% of households — about 740,000 — with no telephone at all in 2025, with 93.8% holding a cellphone only

subject: include.divides
name: KwaZulu-Natal fibre pre-provisioning proof of concept
position_end: Fibre built into the Empangeni Phase 1A housing development for 405 households, with Huawei and Openserve, to test laying connectivity into new settlements as they are built

subject: include.divides
name: Zero-rating of public-benefit websites
position_start: A licence condition on the 2022 spectrum auction requiring operators to zero-rate public-benefit websites, with the regulator's application process gazetted in May 2024
position_end: the obligation acknowledged by the communications minister as moving slowly five months before its deadline, with confidence stated that it will still be met

subject: data.statistics
name: Census 2022
position_end: The country's fourth post-1994 census and its first conducted digitally, counting a population of 62,027,503. The post-enumeration survey put the final net coverage error at 31.1 per cent against a final true in-scope population of 61.4 million, and a 10% sample of the census data was scheduled for release at the end of August 2024
note: three years old at the window's close; the household survey programme redesign reported beside it is what replaces the interval between censuses

subject: data.statistics
name: Census 2031
milestone: Stated as in development by the Presidency, 9 October 2026
position_end: A deputy minister in the Presidency said on 9 October 2026 that Census 2031 is in development, calling statistical independence a constitutional safeguard; the statistics office's parliamentary reply of January 2026 sets a tentative roadmap - strategic planning and budget tabling in 2026/27, frame, consultations and pilots in 2028-2030, main enumeration in October 2031 and a post-enumeration survey in 2031/32 - under a ten-year cycle the 2024 amendment of the Statistics Act made statutory; no budget is held

subject: data.statistics
name: Continuous population survey and household survey redesign
position_end: A frame update for the continuous population survey and household survey programme redesign, the instrument intended to carry population statistics between censuses
note: an undated methodological page; the quarterly labour force survey is the running series it would sit beside, which put unemployment at 33.6% in the second quarter of 2026

subject: data.statistics
name: General Household Survey
position_end: The statistics office's annual household survey, its 2025 edition putting household internet access by any means at 85.6 per cent

subject: data.statistics
name: Insolvencies series
position_start: Suspended since 2021, the administrative supply cut off by a cyber incident at the justice department
position_end: Restored with a first release on 21 July 2026 covering June 2026 and a time series back to January 2023
note: a statistical series lost to a cyber incident in another department and recovered five years later, which is the clearest cost of a security failure on this ledger

subject: data.statistics
name: National Strategy for the Development of Statistics
position_start: Not previously held by this repository
position_end: A strategy to be drafted under a regional statistics project financed by a World Bank concessional arm and run through the regional economic community's secretariat: an expression of interest for an individual consultant to develop South Africa's strategy was issued on 9 September 2026 under reference BW-SADC-563161-CS-INDV.
note: a procurement notice rather than a strategy: no scope, timetable, budget or completion date for the strategy itself is stated, and whether an earlier national statistics strategy exists is not established

subject: data.statistics
name: Price and trade indices built from administrative records
position_end: Sources and methods published for the residential property price index and for the export and import unit value indices, the latter revised in basket and weights effective with the January 2026 index and built from customs administrative records
note: official statistics compiled from another agency's administrative systems, which is what makes them dependent on those systems' continuity

subject: data.statistics
name: Statistics South Africa funding
position_end: The Parliamentary Budget Office put the statistics office's real-terms budget loss at about R750m since 2010, against an R295m the portfolio committee said was urgently needed; the estimates add R208.4m over three years for IT infrastructure and operations

subject: data.statistics
name: Statistics work programme and integrated indicator framework
position_end: 399 of 414 targets achieved for 2025/26 and an integrated indicator framework linking indicators to the national development plan, against a 23% vacancy rate and a R2.2 billion funding shortfall
note: the nearest thing to a national statistical development strategy the repository holds, and the funding shortfall is stated by the office itself

subject: data.statistics
name: Vital statistics releases from civil registration
milestone: Mortality and causes of death 2023 released 25 March 2026
position_end: Statistics South Africa publishes births, marriages and divorces, and deaths from Home Affairs registration records: 863,858 births registered in the 2024 period (released 30 October 2025), 102,373 marriages and unions registered in 2024 and 24,202 divorce forms processed (released 19 March 2026), and 476,605 deaths occurring in 2023 plus 12,580 late registrations for 2002-2022 (released 25 March 2026)
note: The death series runs more than two years behind the year it covers; the next births release is scheduled for 30 November 2026

subject: data.satellite
name: African Meteorological Satellite Application Facility
position_end: Inaugurated under a European-funded project, operationalising satellite-derived nowcasting and impact-based forecasting for African meteorological services, with renewed cooperation agreements approved supporting infrastructure and uptake of third-generation meteorological satellite data
note: a continental facility with South African participation; no domestic user count or forecast product is named

subject: data.satellite
name: AgriWatch regional monitoring dashboard
position_end: A dashboard integrating Earth-observation products for crop-cycle, rangeland-health and rainfall monitoring, with training workshops, shared practice and case studies for government, academic, private-sector and community users across six southern African states
note: no delivery date, hosting arrangement or user count is published

subject: data.satellite
name: Centralised government satellite imagery procurement
position_end: Government satellite-imagery buying moved to a coordinated multi-user licensing model run by the science department and the space agency, with an estimated saving of about R88 million against fragmented purchasing and agriculture among the participating portfolios
note: the saving is the agency's own estimate; no contract, supplier or volume is published

subject: data.satellite
name: GeoMaize satellite crop monitoring
position_end: A satellite-based maize monitoring system in use in two provinces, combining optical and thermal imagery with machine-learning models to push farmer dashboards and text alerts in local languages
note: the agricultural research council's earth observation unit is the standing capability behind it; no user or hectare figure is published

subject: data.satellite
name: SAWIDRA satellite data retransmission station
milestone: Station built under the AfDB programme, reported 2021-07
position_end: One of four regional advanced retransmission stations built under a EUR 20m AfDB programme, downloading meteorological satellite data directly for forecasting and early warning

subject: data.satellite
name: Weather Service satellite, radar and station network
position_end: The Weather Service receives EUMETSAT MSG imagery every 15 minutes and runs 14 radars and 214 automatic weather stations, and was the first in Africa to assimilate regional radar data (2024)

subject: data.satellite
name: Western Cape agricultural commodity mapping
position_end: Provincial agriculture department's mapping of commodity production and infrastructure, with crop field boundaries cleaned, updated and categorised from spatial data

subject: geopol.usa
name: Microsoft cloud and AI investment commitment
status: In development, the company's own figure
milestone: R25.8bn through 2027, restated at a government technology briefing, reported 2026-09-24
position_end: R25.8bn committed to cloud and AI investment in the country through 2027, offered to government with two in-country cloud regions for production and disaster recovery and public, connected-private and disconnected-private deployment options under customer-held keys
note: a vendor's briefing to officials; no delivery or spend-to-date figure is published

subject: geopol.eu
name: European Union science and technology cooperation
position_start: The bilateral agreement in force with no dated meeting on the repository
position_end: The joint science and technology cooperation committee met for the eighteenth time, marking thirty years of the bilateral agreement, with commitments on wider research-programme participation and bilateral artificial-intelligence cooperation
note: commitments rather than an instrument; no value or workstream is published

subject: geopol.eu
name: European Union summit commitments and investment package
milestone: Package of nearly EUR 12 billion announced
position_start: Did not exist on the repository
position_end: A package of nearly EUR 12 billion announced covering digital connectivity among other areas, building on EUR 4.7 billion announced at the March 2025 summit, at which the two sides committed to cooperate on artificial-intelligence governance and the Global Digital Compact
note: the digital share of the package is not itemised, so what reaches connectivity is not derivable from the record

subject: geopol.gulf
name: Gulf-backed satellite connectivity services
position_end: Satellite connectivity services in operation through a domestic venture and a United Arab Emirates operator, using that operator's next-generation and broadband infrastructure and framed against the national broadband programme and rural connectivity
note: no capacity, price, coverage or subscriber figure is published, and no licence instrument is named

subject: geopol.gulf
name: Joint commission with the United Arab Emirates
position_end: The standing bilateral commission with the United Arab Emirates, its second session communique the repository's only record of the relationship's formal machinery
note: eight years old; no later session, memorandum or digital workstream under it is on file

subject: geopol.india
name: Bilateral cooperation with India
milestone: Investment commitments during the deputy president's visit
position_start: A 2016 joint statement as the standing bilateral frame
position_end: Indian industry committed to expanding investment including in information and communications technology during the deputy president's visit, with engagements involving the Indian technology industry association and a trade and technology council
note: commitments by industry rather than by government, with no value or instrument published

subject: geopol.india
name: Provincial engagement on Indian digital procurement
milestone: Provincial treasury engaged the Indian government
position_end: A provincial treasury engaged the Government of India on its government electronic marketplace, drawing on Indian digital public-procurement experience to inform provincial reform
note: knowledge exchange rather than a binding instrument; no memorandum or follow-up is on file
